Edition notice

This publication is intended for operators of cobas® pro
integrated solutions.
Every effort has been made to ensure that all the
information contained in this publication is correct at the
time of publishing. However, the manufacturer of this
product may need to update the publication information
as output of product surveillance activities, leading to a
new version of this publication.

Where to find information

The User Assistance contains all information about the
product, including the following:

The User Guide focuses on routine operation and
maintenance. The chapters are organized according to the
normal operation workflow.
The Safety chapter in this User Guide contains important
safety information. You must read the Safety chapter
before operating the system.
The Quick Reference Guide gives a brief introduction to
important routine tasks and daily maintenance.
The Host Interface Manual provides references for
implementing connections from external laboratory
information systems (LIS) to the product.
cobas® e‑library provides access to Important Notes,
Method Sheets, Value Sheets, and other important
documents from Roche.
The PC manufacturer’s manual contains all information
about the control unit hardware.
The original version of this document is in English. All
translations of this document have been translated from
the original version in English. You can find the original and
translated versions of this document at:
navifyportal.roche.com.
Contact your local affiliate or Roche Service
representative for more information.
cobas® pro integrated solutions can be used with all
released tests. Tests approved for use on the instrument
are available via eLabDoc on the navify® Portal
(navifyportal.roche.com).
Information on globally available accessories,
consumables, current system software version, and
language pack versions can be found online. For ordering
information, contact your local Roche sales representative
or go to eLabDoc on the navify® Portal
(navifyportal.roche.com).
Privacy notice
User Assistance is also available online on the internet.
You can use it independently from the instrument on
Roche Diagnostics
cobas® pro integrated solutions · Software version 03-03 · User Guide · Publication version 4.2

4

computers or mobile devices with a current HTML5
browser. To obtain the appropriate links and usage
information, contact your Roche representative.
When you use User Assistance online, viewing events
(topics viewed and searches performed) and IP addresses
are logged.
The data collected is for Roche internal use only and is
never forwarded to third parties. It is anonymized, and
after 1 year it is automatically deleted.
Viewing events are analyzed to improve User Assistance
content and search functionality. IP addresses are used to
classify regional behavior.
The online User Assistance offers additional features
compared to the one on the system, such as printing,
downloading PDFs, and saving favorites.
General attention
To avoid serious or fatal injury, ensure that you are
familiar with the system and safety information before you
use the system.
r Pay particular attention to all safety precautions.
r Always follow the instructions in this publication.
r Do not use the system in a way that is not described in
this publication.
r Store all publications in a safe and easily retrievable
place.
Incident reporting
r Inform your Roche representative and your local
competent authority about any serious incidents which
may occur when using this product.
Training

Do not perform operation tasks or maintenance actions
unless you have received training from Roche Diagnostics.

Images

The screenshots and hardware images in this publication
have been added exclusively for illustration purposes.
Configurable and variable data in screenshots, such as
tests, results, or path names visible therein must not be
used for laboratory purposes.
Hardware images and screenshots may show an example
for a unit or system configuration.
Content of some hardware images from the utility films
and system explorer may deviate slightly due to a special
instrument model.

Roche-provided hardware firewall

Copyright

License information

License agreement for UltraVNC software

The Roche-provided hardware firewall provides a network
barrier between Roche systems and the customer network
to protect Roche products from network-borne attacks.
•

The use of a Roche-provided hardware firewall is
mandatory.

•

As a key element in the Roche strategy for securing
and protecting its systems, the Roche-provided
hardware firewall must not be removed.

•

The use of the Roche-provided hardware firewall
requires you to assign static IP addresses to Roche
products. The static IP addresses ensure that Roche
products work properly.

15

Intended purpose inside the European Union and EFTA member
states and all countries outside the U.S.
cobas® pro integrated solutions is an automated
analyzer, intended for running qualitative, semiquantitative and quantitative clinical chemistry and
immunochemistry assays as well as ion-selective
measurements.

Supporting information

It is an IVD device intended to be used in combination with
assays for screening, monitoring (aid in monitoring),
diagnosis (aid in diagnosis), and prognosis; additionally,
the device can be used to run companion diagnostic tests.
The specific disorder and testing populations are covered
by the applicable assays running on the instrument. The
type of specimen to be used includes serum, urine, whole
blood, cerebrospinal fluid, supernatant, oral fluid,
hemolysate, amniotic fluid, processed stool and plasma
that are used for detecting and/or measuring analytes
covered by the specific assays.
The intended users of this device are trained laboratory
technicians and trained Roche Service representatives
(professional use only).
Inside the EU/EFTA only, cobas® pro e 801 is also
intended for use in blood donor screening in hospital
blood banks, blood bank laboratories and for blood
donation testing at plasma fractionators.

Intended use statement for U.S. only
cobas® pro integrated solutions is an automated
analyzer, intended for running qualitative, semiquantitative, and quantitative clinical chemistry and
immunochemistry assays as well as ion-selective
measurements.

Supporting information

cobas® pro integrated solutions is intended to be used by
trained laboratory technicians.
Target customers of cobas® pro integrated solutions are
commercial and public clinical laboratories.

Safety classifications
The safety precautions and important user notes are
classified according to the ANSI Z535.6-2011 standard.
Familiarize yourself with the following meanings and icons:
Safety alert
r The safety alert symbol is used to alert you of potential
physical injury hazards. Obey all safety messages that
follow this symbol to avoid possible damage to the
system, injury, or death.
These symbols and signal words are used for specific
hazards:

WARNING!
Warning…
r …indicates a hazardous situation that, if not avoided,
could result in death or serious injury.

CAUTION!
Caution…
r …indicates a hazardous situation that, if not avoided,
could result in minor or moderate injury.

NOTICE!
Notice...
...indicates a hazardous situation that, if not avoided, may
result in damage to the system.

i Tip...

...indicates additional information on correct use or
useful tips.

Safety precautions

Safety precautions
Non-observance of safety precautions
r To avoid serious or fatal injury, read and comply with
the following safety precautions.
The hazard warnings in the user documentation and on the
system cannot cover every possible case, as it is
impossible to predict and evaluate all circumstances
beforehand.
Just following the given directions may, therefore, be
inadequate for operation. Always be alert and use your
common sense.

About operator qualification

1 Safety information

Insufficient knowledge and skills

As an operator, ensure that you know the relevant safety
precaution guidelines and standards, and the information
and procedures contained in these instructions.
r Do not perform operation and maintenance unless a
trainer certified by Roche Diagnostics has trained you
to do so.
r Leave maintenance, installation, or service that is not
described to trained Roche Service representatives.
r Carefully follow the procedures specified in the
instructions for operation and maintenance.
r Follow laboratory best practices, especially when
working with biohazardous material.

About safe and proper use of the system
Missing personal protective equipment

Working without personal protective equipment means
danger to life or health.
r Wear appropriate personal protective equipment,
including, but not limited to, the following items
according to local and laboratory guidelines:
• Eye protection with side shields
• Fluid-resistant lab coat
• Approved lab gloves
• Face shield if there is a chance of splashing or
splattering

System not used for an extended period

r Shut down the system if you do not need it for several
days (up to 17 days). Onboard reagent cooling is still
active. Follow the relevant procedure depending on
the planned shutdown time.
r To switch off the system for more than 17 days,
contact your Roche Service representative. Onboard
reagent cooling is not active. Remove and refrigerate
any remaining reagents.
r For further information, call your Roche Service
representative.

Non‑approved parts

Use of non-approved parts or devices may result in
malfunction of the system and may render the warranty
null and void.
Use of accessories and cables other than specified by the
manufacturer may compromise electromagnetic behavior,
and lead to improper operation.

r Use only accessories and cables specified by Roche
Diagnostics.
Abnormal conditions

During operation, always check for any abnormal sound,
water leakages, or other abnormal conditions.
r If a trouble occurs, take suitable safety measures
according to the condition and contact your Roche
Service representative.

Inappropriate use

Using the system in a way not described by the
manufacturer can impair the protection provided.
r Observe other publications provided for the system.

Power interruption

31

A power failure or momentary drop in voltage may
damage the system or lead to data loss.
r Operate only with an uninterruptible power supply
(UPS) that meets the required standards and
regulations.
r For installing a UPS, refer to the corresponding
instruction manual. If there are any questions, contact
the UPS manufacturer or the distributor.
r Do not install the software that comes with the UPS.
r Do not connect the USB cable or communication cable
that comes with the UPS to the control unit PC.
r Do not modify the power cable plug when connecting it
to the UPS.
r It is recommended to check if the selected UPS
operates and backs up properly before use.
r Perform regular backups of results or enable the
sample records management as a self-operating
maintenance.
r The backup time of the UPS is limited. If the power
outage is expected to continue more than the backup
time, shut down in advance.
r Ensure periodic maintenance of the UPS.
r Do not switch off power while the control unit PC
accesses the hard disk or a storage medium.

About installation and deinstallation
Only trained Roche Service representatives may install
the system.
r Leave installation that is not described to trained
Roche Service representatives.
Damage in transit

r Do not attempt to relocate or transport the system.
r Leave relocation and transportation to Roche Service
representatives.

Disposal

A biohazardous system may lead to infection.
r If you must dispose of the system, read the information
about disposal in this publication.
u Disposal information (85)

Safety precautions

About the protection of personal data and software
security
The General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) is a
regulation in EU law on data protection and privacy for all
citizens of the European Union (EU) and the European
Economic Area (EEA). The regulation also covers the
processing of personal data outside the EU and EEA
areas.
If this regulation or any other privacy protection regulation
is applicable for your country, observe the following safety
messages to prevent data breaches and to meet the
GDPR:
Access control

Unauthorized access may lead to data breaches.
r Implement physical access controls to ensure that only
authorized laboratory staff operate the system at all
times.
r Assign a personal, unique user ID to each user for
system access.
r Assign access rights to each user only as high as
required for the tasks of the user.
r Delete user IDs from the system for users who no
longer work on the system.
r Restrict user access to ensure that users do not
change PC settings.

Corrupt data due to a disclosed password

The security of the system and its data depends on the
password-protected access. If an unauthorized person
discovers your user ID and password, they could
compromise this security.

1 Safety information

r Always enter your password unobserved.
r Do not write down your password anywhere, including
in a contact form, in the address book, or in a file on
the computer.
r Do not disclose your password to anyone. Roche will
never ask you for your password.
r If you ever disclose your password to anyone, change it
immediately afterwards.
r Contact your local Roche affiliate if you think your
account has been compromised.

Roche Diagnostics
cobas® pro integrated solutions · Software version 03-03 · User Guide · Publication version 4.2

Safety information

Network security

33

Malicious software and hacker attacks may impair IT
security. The laboratory is responsible for the IT security
of their IT infrastructure.
r To protect and separate Roche systems from other
laboratory infrastructure, the Roche-provided firewall
must be used.
r Secure all devices and services used in the laboratory
infrastructure against malicious software and
unauthorized access.
r Secure the network environment to be resilient against
traffic redirection and eavesdropping.

Data entry and data transfer

Writing patient sensitive information in comment fields
can violate protection laws for protected health
information.
r Do not write any patient sensitive information into
comment fields.
r Do not download patient identifiers from any host
system (e.g., LIS, middleware, or HIS) onto the system.
Data transfer using any host protocol (e.g., HL7)
usually is not encrypted; data is transferred as
plaintext and readable with IT tools. Roche strongly
recommends using encrypted communication with the
host system.

Secure data storage

Unauthorized access to data backups and archive files
can violate data protection laws.
r Any data backup or data archive that has been
exported from the instrument must be physically
stored in a secured location.

r Data backups must not be taken from the secure data
storage. Do not take storage media outside the
laboratory environment.

cobas® pro integrated solutions · Software version 03-03 · User Guide · Publication version 4.2

1 Safety information

r Ensure only authorized persons may access the secure
data storage. This includes the data transfer to remote
storage locations and disaster recovery.

Cybersecurity and privacy awareness

Insufficiently informed employees can endanger security.
r Perform regular cybersecurity and privacy awareness
trainings for laboratory staff handling personal data.
Instruct laboratory staff how to handle data in a

as mandated by customer regulations.

report it immediately to your local Roche
representative.
r Update to the latest software versions provided by
Roche as soon as possible.
r Do not use external storage devices or storage media
(e.g., USB flash drives) on the system that have been
used on public or private computers. Failure to do so
may result in data loss and render the instrument
unusable.

loss or system malfunction.

from the system using the
button.

is in use.

Biohazardous materials
Sharps, rough edges, and/or moving parts

Some areas of the instrument may have sharps, rough
edges, and/or moving parts. Contact with such parts may
lead to personal injury or infection. Good laboratory
practice can reduce the risk of injury.
r Be aware of your laboratory environment, wellprepared, and follow the instructions for use.

1 Safety information

r Wear personal protective equipment to minimize the
risk of injury from bodily contact with such parts,
especially in less accessible areas, or while cleaning
the instrument.
r Use personal protective equipment appropriate to the
degree and type of potential hazard, e.g., suitable lab
gloves, eye protection, lab coat, and footwear.

Infectious samples

37

Contact with samples containing material of human origin
may result in infection. All materials and mechanical
components associated with samples containing material
of human origin are potentially infectious.
r Follow laboratory best practices, especially when
working with biohazardous material.
r Keep all covers closed and in place.
r Before you work with an opened cover, always switch
off the system or choose a mode appropriate for the
particular maintenance action.
r Wear appropriate personal protective equipment.
r If any biohazardous material is spilled, wipe it up
immediately and apply a disinfectant.
r If sample or waste comes into contact with your skin,
wash the affected area immediately with soap and
water and apply a disinfectant.
Consult a physician.

Spilled sample

The sample containers may vibrate during rack transport
leading to sample spillage on the transport mechanisms.
r Avoid overfilling sample tubes and cups.
r Only use specified sample tubes and cups.
r Leave approximately 10 mm clearance between the
liquid and the top of the sample tube or cup.
r After loading the rack trays on the input buffer, move
the racks to the front of the tray, so that there is no
gap between the individual racks.

Ultrasonic mixers and sonic wash stations

Contact with splashes or inhalation of aerosol from the
ultrasonic mixer or sonic wash station may result in
infection.
r Keep all covers closed and in place.

Warning messages

Moving parts

Contact with moving parts may result in infection or
personal injury.
r Keep all covers closed and in place.
r Before you work with an opened cover, always switch
off the system or choose a mode appropriate for the
particular maintenance action.
r Do not touch any parts of the system except those
parts specified. Keep away from moving parts during
operation.
r Only load or unload racks when the green status
indicators at the rack input buffer are lighting.
r During operation and maintenance, carefully follow the
instructions.
r Only trained personnel should have access to the keys
for the covers of the system.

Sharp objects

Contact with probes or rack trays may result in infection.
r When you wipe probes, use several layers of gauze and
wipe from the top down.
r When you wipe rack trays, avoid contact with all sharp
edges, even when wearing lab gloves.
r Take care not to puncture yourself.
r Wear appropriate personal protective equipment.
r Take extra care when working with lab gloves, which
can easily be pierced or cut, leading to infection.

Waste

1 Safety information

Infectious waste

Contact with waste (liquid and/or solid) may result in
infection. All materials and mechanical components
associated with the waste systems are potentially
infectious.
r Wear appropriate personal protective equipment.
r Take extra care when working with lab gloves. They can
easily be pierced or cut, leading to infection.
r If any biohazardous material is spilled, wipe it up
immediately and apply a disinfectant.
r If waste comes into contact with your skin, wash the
affected area immediately with soap and water and
apply a disinfectant.
Consult a physician.
Waste must be treated in accordance with the relevant
laws and local regulations. Any substances contained in
reagents, calibrators, and QC materials, which are legally

Roche Diagnostics
cobas® pro integrated solutions · Software version 03-03 · User Guide · Publication version 4.2

Safety information

39

regulated for environmental protection, must be disposed
of according to the relevant water discharge facility
regulations. For the legal regulations on water discharge,
contact local authorities.
The system discharges 2 kinds of liquid waste:

Harmful fumes

•

Highly concentrated waste: Liquid waste that contains
highly concentrated reaction mixtures. This waste
must be treated as infectious waste as specified by
the relevant regulations.

•

Diluted waste (CC analytical units): Liquid waste
diluted with rinsing water from the reaction cell wash
or water from the incubation bath. When using Basic
Wash for washing the reaction cells, alkaline
concentration is 0.1–1.0 mmol/L.

•

Diluted waste (e 801): Liquid waste diluted with rinsing
water from washing the probes, nozzles, and other
components that were in contact with sample
material.

The combination of bleach with the contents of the liquid
waste container can cause potentially harmful fumes.
r Do not use bleach to clean the liquid waste container.

Environmental harm

The system generates liquid and/or solid waste. This
waste contains concentrated reaction solutions and is
potentially biohazardous. Improper disposal may
contaminate the environment.
r Treat this waste as infectious waste.
r Dispose of waste in accordance with the local
regulations.

Accuracy and precision

Incorrect results may lead to errors in diagnosis, posing
danger to the patient.
r For proper use of the system, run QC tests regularly
and monitor the system during operation.
r Do not use reagents or consumables that have
exceeded their expiration date or onboard stability,
otherwise you may obtain inaccurate data.
r For diagnostic purposes, always assess the results with
the patient’s medical history, clinical examination, and
results from other consultations.

Warning messages

Regular cleaning and maintenance

To prevent inaccurate results and unsafe operation of the
system:
r Regularly clean and/or decontaminate the system as
required. Follow laboratory best practices for cleaning
and decontamination.
r Ensure that the laboratory is regularly cleaned and is
maintained in an orderly manner.
r Perform the maintenance actions according to the
given maintenance intervals.

Sample container and racks

The system derives the sample container geometry by
rack ID. Placing a sample container on a rack that is not
defined for this sample container may cause damage to
the sample probe during sampling. A damaged sample
probe may lead to inaccurate pipetting and incorrect
results.
r Load sample containers on racks according to the
assigned rack range for the sample container and
sample type.
r When using standard cups or micro cups, select the
correct cup size.
r Do not mix non-standard tubes, false-bottom tubes,
and standard tubes on one rack.

Sample mismatch in non-barcode mode

Placing a sample container on a wrong position may lead
to incorrect results.
r When operating in non-barcode mode, make sure that
you register the samples in the same order as they
were ordered.
r Take care when you work in non-barcode mode
because of the risk of sample mismatch.
r Do not exchange or remove samples.

1 Safety information

Foam, clots, films, or air bubbles

Incorrect results may occur due to foam, fibrin clots,
films, or air bubbles in reagents or samples.
r Avoid the formation of foam, clots, and air bubbles in
all reagents, samples, calibrators, and QC materials.

Contaminated samples

Insoluble contaminants, air bubbles, or films in samples
may cause clogging or pipetting volume shortage, leading
to incorrect results.
r Ensure that the samples contain no insoluble
contaminants, such as fibrin or gel.
r Ensure to prepare enough pipetting volume for
measurement.

Roche Diagnostics
cobas® pro integrated solutions · Software version 03-03 · User Guide · Publication version 4.2

Safety information

Sample contamination

41

If liquid or particles get inside the sample supply unit,
samples may become contaminated.
r Keep the cover of the sample supply unit closed while
the instrument is operating.
r Do not place anything on the cover of the sample
supply unit.

Evaporation of reagents

Evaporation of reagents may lead to incorrect results.
r Do not use improperly stored reagents. Ensure that
reagents are stored according to the Instructions for
Use.

Incorrect reagent volume

Incorrect reagent handling may cause an undetectable
loss of reagent.
r Always store reagents according to the specified
storage conditions as stated in the Method Sheet for
the test.
r Reload a reagent pack only if you are sure that the
reagent volumes remained unchanged while the
reagent pack was not on the system.
r Do not reload a reagent pack or a system reagent
bottle whose reagent has spilled.
r Do not use a reagent pack or system reagent bottle on
different systems.
r Never refill a reagent pack. Discard empty reagent
packs.

Incorrect reagent filling volume – CC
analytical units

Filling the CDC cobas® c pack green incorrectly may
cause a reagent shortage and lead to incorrect results.
r Fill the CDC cobas® c pack green according to the
Method Sheet.

Expired reagents or mixing reagents

Data obtained using expired reagents is not reliable.
Mixing new reagents with residues of old reagents may
also lead to incorrect results.
r Do not use reagents that have exceeded their
expiration date or onboard stability, otherwise you may
obtain inaccurate data.
r Do not mix old reagents with new reagents.
When the system indicates a bottle is empty, replace it
with a new one.

Warning messages

Contaminated reagents

Cleaning fluid or cleaning devices may enter through the
reagent pipetting openings during maintenance, which
leads to incorrect results.
r Place a paper towel over the reagent pipetting holes
during maintenance.
r During maintenance, carefully follow the instructions.

Incorrect temperature of reagents

Incorrect temperature of reagents may lead to incorrect
results and influences the onboard stability of reagents.
r Keep all covers closed and in place.
r During operation and maintenance, carefully follow the
instructions.
r During loading of reagent packs, observe all alarms.
r If an error occurs, resolve the loading issue or put the
reagent pack back into the refrigerator.

Calibrators or QC materials

Data obtained using the calibrators and QC materials
inappropriately is not reliable.
r Do not use calibrators or QC materials that have
exceeded the stability of their components after
reconstitution according to the Method Sheet.
r Do not mix up calibrator containers or QC material
containers.
r Do not use calibrator set points or QC values from a
different lot.

QC target values

Editing QC target values may cause incorrect QC results
and lead to incorrect sample results.

1 Safety information

r For QC material provided by Roche Diagnostics: Do not
edit QC target values unless Roche Diagnostics
instructs you to do so.
r Take extra care when you edit QC target values.
Ensure that you enter current and valid values for the
target mean and standard deviation for the used QC
lot.
Expired ISE electrodes

Data obtained using expired ISE electrodes is not reliable.
r Do not use ISE electrodes that have exceeded their
expiration date or onboard stability.

Roche Diagnostics
cobas® pro integrated solutions · Software version 03-03 · User Guide · Publication version 4.2

Safety information

Missing covers of the ISE analytical unit

43

If the covers of the electrode block are not reinstalled
after maintenance, the temperature and/or noise level
may be affected, leading to incorrect results. Touching
any ISE component or opening the front doors may also
affect the noise level and lower measurement precision.
r Only perform measurements if the covers of the ISE
analytical unit are installed.
r Do not open the front doors or covers during
measurement.
r Do not touch components of the ISE analytical unit
during measurement.

Undetected barcode reading errors

Barcode reading errors can potentially go undetected
when a check digit is not used.
r Use only barcodes with check digits.
r Use only barcode labels of a good printout quality.
r Place barcode labels in appropriate position and
orientation on the sample containers.
r Do not move any samples that have already been
scanned.
r Do not add a non‑barcoded sample into the position of
a sample with an unreadable barcode.

Sample mismatch due to rack ID scanning
errors

In the event of a scan error of the rack ID, the instrument
may mismatch samples. Mismatched samples lead to
incorrect results.
r Check the rack barcodes before each use.
r Make sure that the barcode labels are clean,
undamaged, and readable.
r Clean the racks regularly.

Carryover - CC

Traces of reagents may be carried over from one test to
the next.
r Take adequate measures (for example, extra wash
cycles) to avoid extra testing and potentially incorrect
results.

Shortage and misplacement

Shortage or misplacement of reagent bottles may result
in delayed results, instrument error, or sample loss.
r Ensure correct placement and sufficient supply of the
reagent bottles.

Electrical safety
Electric shock

Removing the covers of electronic equipment can cause
electric shock because there are high‑voltage parts
inside.
r Do not attempt to work on any electronic equipment.
r Do not remove any cover of the system except those
covers specified in the instructions.
r Do not open the main cover and touch the ultrasonic
mixing unit during operation or when the system
performs maintenance.
r Only Roche Service representatives may install,
service, and repair the system.

Immediate action in an emergency situation

If an unexpected emergency situation appears and the
system cannot be controlled, this can lead to injury of the
operator.
r Turn off the main circuit breaker or the circuit breaker
of the affected analytical unit.
r Disconnect the power supply cords of all units.

1 Safety information

r If a generic emergency situation appears that cannot
be allocated to a specific analytical unit, turn off the
power supply of the sample supply unit.

Electromagnetic compatibility
Electromagnetic compatibility

The instrument complies with the emission and immunity
requirements described in standard IEC 61326-2-6/
EN 61326-2-6.
It has been designed and tested to CISPR 11 Class A. In a
domestic environment it may cause radio interference, in
which case, you must take measures to mitigate the
interference.
The RFID readers in the system comply with the emission
requirements described in this part of the FCC CFR 47,
Part 15 Class A.
Nevertheless, high frequency waves and other
electromagnetic disturbances may lead to incorrect
results, safety problems, operational interruptions, or
instrument damage.
Using this instrument in a dry environment may cause
electrostatic discharges and voltage spikes, which may
lead to incorrect results and damages.
Emission: This instrument can radiate radio frequency
energy. If not installed and used in accordance with the
instructions, it may cause harmful interference to other
equipment in the proximity.
r Ensure that the instrument is only used in a safe
electromagnetic environment before operating the
instrument.

r Do not operate any radio frequency communication
devices that generate electromagnetic fields (e.g.
mobile phones, transceivers, cordless phones) close to
the instrument (30 cm/12 inches or less).
r If other equipment must be operated next to the
instrument, verify that this instrument and the other
equipment are functioning normally.
Ensure that the other equipment complies with
IEC 61326-1, IEC 61326-2-6, or IEC 60601-1-2.
r Do not operate the instrument in a dry environment
(30% humidity or less).
r Do not operate the instrument when synthetic
materials are present (synthetic clothing, carpets,
etc.).

Roche Diagnostics
cobas® pro integrated solutions · Software version 03-03 · User Guide · Publication version 4.2

1 Safety information

r Do not operate this instrument close to sources of
strong electromagnetic fields (for example, unshielded
intentional radio frequency sources). Such fields may
interfere with proper operations.

76

Safety information for barcode readers

Safety information for barcode readers
The system uses barcode readers to read the barcodes on
sample tubes and racks.
•

Most of the barcode readers use LED technology with
low output power.

•

One laser barcode reader is used in the sample supply
unit. The laser beam is fully covered during normal
operation.

The mentioned classes refer to the standard
IEC 60825-1:2014:
•

Class 1: Eye-safe under normal environmental
conditions.

•

Class 2: Visible lasers. Eye-safe for accidental viewing.
However, it may not be safe for a person who
deliberately stares into the laser beam for longer than
0.25 s by overcoming their natural aversion response
to the bright light.

In this section
About the laser barcode reader – cobas® pro sample
supply unit, Mat. No. 08464502001 (76)
About the laser barcode reader – cobas® pro SSU,
Mat. No. 09205632001 (78)

1 Safety information

About the laser barcode reader – cobas® pro sample
supply unit, Mat. No. 08464502001
The sample supply unit uses a barcode reader to identify
the barcodes on sample tubes.
The barcode reader uses a covered laser beam.
The sample supply unit is a Class 1 product because the
beam of the used class 2 laser is protected from possible
viewing.

without starting operation.

1 Safety information

During operation, you cannot open covers with a safety
interlock.
For loading reagent packs in Standby mode, the main
cover must be closed.

Using maintenance mode – c 503
To check the horizontal alignment of the probes, use the
maintenance mode. The maintenance mode allows the
mechanical parts to move while covers with safety
interlock are open. The safety interlock is switched off.

Use the Maintenance Mode key to release the safety
interlock. Insert the Maintenance Mode key at the rear of
the c 503 analytical unit.
When the system is in maintenance mode, the switch-on
process will not be performed correctly. Before you switch
the system on, ensure the system is not in the
Maintenance Mode position.

WARNING!

A

Infection and injury due to contact with system
mechanisms

A Maintenance Mode key – c 503

mechanisms may lead to biohazardous contamination,
resulting in personal injury and/or infection.

covers are closed and locked.
r Before working with open covers, put the system or the
corresponding analytical unit into an appropriate
mode. The appropriate modes are described in the
prerequisites of the maintenance instruction.

parts specified.

Safety information

85

Safety information for disposal
Disposal information
r Treat the system as infectious waste. This applies to all
units except the control unit components.
Decontamination (the combination of processes
including cleaning, disinfection, and/or sterilization) is
required before reuse, recycling, or disposal of the
system.

Infection by an infectious system

r After decontamination, still treat the system as
potentially infectious as there might be a remaining
risk.
r Dispose of the system according to the local
regulations. For more information, contact your Roche
Service representative.
Collection of fluorocarbons

The cooling units in the analytical units contain
fluorocarbons. In some countries, fluorocarbons must be
disposed of by designated collection facilities.
r For the disposal of the cooling unit, refer to local
regulations and authorities.
•

Do not discard devices marked with the crossed-out
wheeled bin symbol as unsorted mixed household
waste. Send these devices to separate facilities for
recovery and recycling.

•

Before disposal, ensure that any liquid or solid waste
is removed from the devices.

•

Before disposal, disinfect the exterior of the devices
with a disinfectant solution recommended in these
instructions.

•

If applicable, before disposal, remove used batteries
and accumulators.

•

If applicable, before disposal, ensure that personal
data is deleted from the device.

•

These devices must be disposed of at collection
facilities designated by government or local
authorities. Avoid sending EEE components to landfill.

•

For more information on how to dispose of your old
device, contact your city office, your waste disposal
service, or your Roche Service representative.

•

Constraint: It is left to the responsible laboratory
organization to determine whether the devices are
contaminated or not. If contaminated, treat them in
the same way as biologically contaminated/hazardous
waste.

About the system
cobas® pro integrated solutions is a fully automated
laboratory system for the measurement of analytes in
body fluids.
The system simplifies the workflow by further automating
labor-intensive tasks such as maintenance and reagent
handling.
cobas® pro integrated solutions has a modular design
which means that different combinations of analytical
units are available.

About cobas® link software

Roche digital infrastructure

The Roche-provided gateway (cobas® link/Unified
Gateway) provides a secure remote connection for data
transfer between the cobas® systems in your laboratory
and the Roche digital infrastructure.
The gateway is used to access the e-library to view
Method Sheets, Value Sheets for calibrators and QC
materials, and other documents.

Roche-provided gateway

Other functionalities provided by the gateway are:
•

System

Automatic synchronization of recent parameters from
the remote service platform to your system (once per
day and during power-up of the system):
– Applications
– Calibrators
– QC materials
– Reagents
– Special wash rules

•

Archiving of Instructions for Use.

•

Uploading of statistical data from your system to the
remote service platform:
– Monitor performance
– QC management
– Service purposes

Content of e-library
For each application, calibrator, and QC material, the elibrary contains the latest version of the respective
e‑library package and the preceding version. Any older
e‑library packages are deleted from the e-library.

updated daily via an automatic download from the remote
service platform.

available for download from the e-library.

About overdraw volume
The sample probe aspirates a slightly larger volume than it
dispenses into the reaction cell. This overdraw volume is
discarded.
The sample probes on the following analytical units
aspirate overdraw volume:
•

ISE analytical unit

•

CC analytical unit
Analytical unit

Overdraw volume

ISE v1

10 µL

ISE neo

7.5 µL

c 503

7.5 µL

c 703

7.5 µL

y Overdraw volume

The overdraw volume is kept during repeated aspiration of
the same patient sample, calibrator, or QC material.

2 Overview of the system

The overdraw volume is discarded when a cell-to-cell
transfer occurs during repeated aspiration. After each
cell-to-cell transfer, the overdraw volume is renewed.

About loading samples
When loading samples ensure that the tubes and barcodes
are correctly aligned on the rack.

Correct alignment of sample tubes on a rack

2 Overview of the system

A

A Incorrect—sample
tube misaligned

Take special care to place sample tubes correctly onto
the rack.

For correct sampling, the position of the sample tube must
be vertically as straight as possible and fully inserted in
the racks. If sample tubes are not in a correct upright
position or not fully inserted in the rack, the sample probe
might hit the inside of the sample tube. This would result in
incorrect liquid level detection (LLD) and air aspiration.
The vertical position also reduces possible barcode
reading errors and incorrect pipettings.

B

B Correct—sample tube
vertically aligned

Readability of barcodes

Correct placement is especially important for sample
tubes with a diameter of 13 mm or less.

To prevent barcode read errors, it is necessary to stick the
barcode labels on the tubes correctly and to align the
tubes in the rack correctly.

Roche Diagnostics
cobas® pro integrated solutions · Software version 03-03 · User Guide · Publication version 4.2

In accordance with laboratory best practices, observe the
following:
•

To avoid sample contamination, keep the cover of the
sample supply unit closed during routine procedures.

•

Ensure the correct position of all barcode labels on
racks to minimize errors during barcode readings.

•

Ensure the correct orientation of the racks and the
rack tray. Racks are placed onto a tray with the aid of
a guiding rail. The narrow end of the racks and the
rack tray handle must be on the right.

•

Always move rack trays with care, to prevent splashing
between samples and thus carryover.

•

After loading the rack trays on the input buffer, move
the racks to the front of the tray, so that there is no
gap between the individual racks.

About using different sample types on the same rack

2 Overview of the system

Placing samples of different sample types on the same
rack can be useful, for example, if the instrument is
connected to a laboratory automation system (LAS). The
LAS can use the same rack range for pre-processing
different sample types.
If a sample is loaded on a rack assigned to sample type
urine, for instance, the system assumes that all samples in
this rack are urine samples. If there is a host connection,
the sample type assigned by the system has to fit the
sample type in the host otherwise the sample is not
processed. Likewise a manually programmed serum/
plasma sample can only be measured on a rack assigned
for this sample type. In order to reach sample type
consolidation, i.e. loading different sample types on the
same rack, certain rules have to be followed.

About barcode and non‑barcode mode
In barcode mode, the system uses barcodes to identify
samples. In non-barcode mode, the system assigns a
sequence number to the loaded samples. You must
organize this sequence of the samples manually or with
your host to track the samples’ identities.

2 Overview of the system

Barcode mode

Barcodes are used for identifying patient samples,
calibrators, and QC materials. In barcode mode, the
barcode on the sample container represents the sample
ID.
Barcodes for samples can be generated by your
laboratory-wide barcode labeling and printing system.
Barcodes for calibrators and QC materials are supplied
with the respective calibrators and QC materials.
To avoid the risk of sample mismatch, Roche recommends
operating the system in barcode mode.
If the barcode mode is activated under Menu > System >
Barcode Reading, it is still possible to process samples
without barcodes. In this case, under Routine > Order
Tests use the No Barcode check box to enter a rack ID
and rack position for these samples.
If non-barcoded samples have been aliquoted on a
laboratory automation system, the barcode mode is also
used. In this case, the system receives the sample ID, rack
ID, and rack position number together with the test order.
Also calibrators and QC materials can be used without
barcodes using rack assignment.

Roche Diagnostics
cobas® pro integrated solutions · Software version 03-03 · User Guide · Publication version 4.2

Overview of the system

Non-barcode mode

121

The system uses an internal worklist to track the sequence
of samples. On the worklist, samples are sequentially
numbered and assigned to racks by rack ID and rack
position.
You can generate a worklist manually by ordering tests on
the Order Tests submenu and entering a sample
sequence number. The worklist can also be generated by
the host.
The Test Order list represents the internal worklist.
The system uses only the sample sequence number to
identify samples. Optionally, you can still assign a sample
ID, which can be text, to help identify samples.

• Registering a sample with unreadable (or without)

Barcode labels are used to identify:
•

Patient samples (1D or 2D)

•

Calibrators

•

QC materials

•

Racks

Only use barcodes with check digit to avoid undetected
errors during barcode reading. Undetected barcode
reading errors can lead to sample mismatch. Ensure that
the barcode labels are clean, dry, and in clear print. When
fixing barcode labels on sample tubes, ensure that the
barcode image lies within the barcode scan zone. Avoid
tilted barcode labels.
Barcode labels cannot be placed on cups. If you must
identify a cup by barcode, use a cup on a tube and label
the respective tube with a barcode. Alternatively, you can
use a false-bottom tube for small volume samples.

About the sample supply unit
At the sample supply unit, you can switch on the system,
manage processes with the touch screen, and access the
PC. Use the sample supply unit also to load and unload
sample racks, calibrator racks, and QC racks.
The sample supply unit controls and optimizes the rack
movements throughout the whole instrument.

Unloading lanes

The unloading lanes consist of 2 lanes each holding up to
30 racks (150 samples). The unloading lanes hold
processed racks until you remove them from the
instrument.

Main cover

The main cover protects samples from contamination. Do
not open the main cover if the status indicators are off.

Loading lanes

The loading lanes consist of 2 lanes each holding up to
30 racks (150 samples). The racks can be put into the
loading lane on rack trays holding up to 15 racks. The
racks are transported towards the rear buffer of the
respective lane. As soon as a rack tray is empty, the status
indicator turns green. Then you can open the main cover
and replace the empty rack tray with a full rack tray.

A

136

About the core unit

Sample barcode reader

The sample barcode reader scans the barcode of each
tube. To avoid barcode read errors, ensure that the
barcode labels are clean, dry, and in clear print. When
fixing barcode labels on tubes, ensure that the barcode
lies within the barcode scan zone. Avoid tilted barcode
labels and tubes.

Rack barcode reader

The rack barcode reader scans the barcode rack IDs to
identify the racks. Samples (routine samples, STAT
samples, calibrators, or QC materials) must be transported
on racks of the corresponding rack type. Each rack type
has its own color and ID range.

Status indicators

The status indicators indicate whether you can access a
lane of the loading or unloading area.
•

ON: Lane is accessible

•

OFF: No access

Power panel and drain tubing of degasser are located behind the front door

Power panel

The system is shut down via the user interface. When it has
shut down, power is still supplied to the cooling units of
the analytical units.
The system is intended for continuous operation (24/7).
However, you can also shut down the system at the end of
a shift and start it up automatically using a timer before
the next shift. In this case, while the system has shut down,
the display on the power panel displays the next set wakeup time. For example, when the display reads "16 06:00",
the instrument will wake up at 06:00 on the 16th of the
month.

About the core unit

STAT port
At the STAT port, you can load any rack directly onto the
transport line. Racks loaded at the STAT port are
processed with higher priority than sample racks loaded
via the loading area.
If the instrument is connected to a laboratory automation
system, the STAT port becomes the main input location for
racks. The loading lanes take over the functionality of the
STAT port.
Circuit breaker
The circuit breaker protects the system from damage from
excess current. For troubleshooting, Roche Service
representatives may advise you to use the circuit breaker
to switch off all the power to the system, including the
reagent disk cooling unit.

The sample buffers receive racks from the sample supply
unit via the transport line. The sample buffers keep the
racks until they are due for sample pipetting in at least one
of the analytical units.

buffers can deliver racks to any analytical unit at any time.

lane of the sample supply unit via the rack return line at
the back of the instrument.

About the ISE v1 analytical unit

About the ISE v1 analytical unit
The ISE v1 analytical unit uses 3 ion-selective electrodes
and a reference electrode to determine the concentration
of the respective ions in diluted samples:
•

Sodium (Na+)

•

Potassium (K+)

•

Chloride (Cl-)

The ISE v1 analytical unit has a throughput of 900 tests/h.

3 Overview of the instrument

The ISE v1 analytical unit shares the sample buffer with
the c 503 analytical unit to the right of the sample buffer.
The c 503 analytical unit supplies water, vacuum, and
Basic Wash solution to the associated ISE v1 analytical
unit.

Pipetting position

The rack transport line transports racks into the ISE v1
analytical unit until the first tube on the rack is in the
pipetting position. Then the sample pipetter aspirates
sample.

Sonic wash station

Every 150 pipettings, after identification of a sample clot
as well as during Preparation and Post Operation
mode, the sample probe is washed inside and outside with
Basic Wash solution and ultrasound.

Rinse station

To prevent carryover, the sample probe is rinsed inside
and outside with deionized water before each aspiration.

Dispensing position

At the dispensing position, the dilution vessel receives the
sample from the sample pipetter.

Drain port

The liquid waste from the ISE v1 analytical unit drains into
the drain port.

Dilution vessel

In the dilution vessel, the sample is mixed with ISE Diluent
according to the application settings specified in the
corresponding application file. The mixture is aspirated
into the ISE electrodes and measured.

ISE sipper

This nozzle aspirates ISE Internal Standard solution or
diluted sample from the dilution vessel into the electrode
block.

ISE electrodes, ISE reference electrode

The diluted sample is aspirated from the dilution vessel
into the ISE electrodes. ISE Reference Electrolyte solution
is aspirated from the respective bottle behind the front
door through the ISE reference electrode.

Pinch valve

The pinch valve is involved in controlling the liquid flow
through the ISE electrodes.

About the ISE neo analytical unit

Electrode block – ISE neo
The ISE neo analytical unit has 1 or 2 identical
temperature-controlled compartments with 3 ion-selective
electrodes and 1 ISE reference electrode for each
measuring unit. The concentration of Na+, K+, and Cl- in the
diluted sample is determined from the potential
differences between the ion-selective electrodes and the
ISE reference electrode.

Sample pipetter (S1)

This sample pipetter aspirates patient sample, calibrator,
or QC material from containers on the racks and dispenses
the material into an empty reaction cell on the reaction
disk. The sample pipetter has liquid level detection, clot
detection, and air aspiration detection. A sample can be
dispensed every 3.6 s. While dispensing, the beveled tip of
the sample probe touches the bottom of the reaction cell
to ensure a precise dispense volume. The sample probe is
spring-mounted to avoid damage to the probe and to the
reaction cells.

Sample pipetter (S2)

This sample pipetter is used only for whole blood testing. It
aspirates patient sample, calibrator, and QC material from
sample containers on the racks and dispenses the material
into an empty reaction cell on the reaction disk. The
sample pipetter has clot detection.

C Reagent pipetter (R2/3)
Reagent pipetters

The reagent pipetters are mounted on 2 independent
x‑y‑mechanisms. The reagent pipetters aspirate reagent
from the reagent packs and dispense the reagent into
reaction cells in the reaction disk area. Each reagent
pipetter serves specific reagent timings (R1 or R2/R3).
The reagent pipetters have liquid level detection, clot
detection and air aspiration detection. The reagent
pipetters are connected to reagent syringes, which are
located behind the front doors of the instrument.

Photometer lamp

The light of the photometer lamp passes through a glass
window into the incubation bath. In the incubation bath, it
passes through the reaction cell and the reaction mixture.
Then, the light passes through another glass window into
the photometer. The photometer measures the
absorbance of the reaction mixture. The system
determines the concentration of the analyte from the
measurements and the respective calibration curve.

Roche Diagnostics
cobas® pro integrated solutions · Software version 03-03 · User Guide · Publication version 4.2

3 Overview of the instrument

A

3 Overview of the instrument

182

About the c 503 analytical unit

Reaction cells wash unit

After measuring, the wash unit cleans, rinses, and dries the
reaction cells. For cleaning, Basic Wash solution and/or
Acid Wash solution are used, depending on the test
previously measured in the reaction cell. For rinsing,
deionized water is used. After cleaning and rinsing, 3 cell
blank measurements are performed to verify the optical
performance of the reaction cell. If the result deviates
significantly from the previous cell blank measurement,
the reaction cell is disabled.

Reaction cells

The sample material and the reagents are dispensed into
the reaction cells. The solution in each reaction cell is
mixed, incubated, and measured. The reaction disk holds
13 segments with 17 reaction cells per segment. You must
replace used segments monthly.

Ultrasonic mixers

The 3 ultrasonic mixers are used for non‑contact mixing of
the reaction mixture in the reaction cells. Each ultrasonic
mixer is assigned to 1 of the 3 reagent timings R1, R2,
or R3. For automatic sample dilutions, R1 is used.

Reaction disk

The reaction disk has 221 reusable plastic reaction cells.
The reaction disk turns the reaction cells to the sample
pipetter, reagent pipetters, ultrasonic mixers, photometer
window, and reaction cells wash unit.

Incubation bath

The reaction cells are immersed in an incubation bath to
maintain the reaction mixture at the required temperature
of 37 °C ± 0.1 °C. A liquid level sensor controls the water
level of the incubation bath and triggers the adding of
deionized water to compensate for evaporation.
EcoTergent is an additive to the incubation bath that
minimizes the formation of air bubbles which could
interfere with the photometer readings. It also adds
conductivity for the water level sensor and prevents
bacterial and algae growth.

Sampling area – c 703

192

About the c 703 analytical unit

Sample pipetters (SA & SB)

The sample pipetters aspirate patient sample, calibrator,
or QC material from containers on the racks and dispenses
the material into an empty reaction cell on the reaction
disk. The sample pipetters have liquid level detection, clot
detection, and air aspiration detection. A sample can be
dispensed every 1.8 s. While dispensing, the beveled tip of
the sample probe touches the bottom of the reaction cell
to ensure a precise dispense volume. The sample probes
are spring-mounted to avoid damage to the probe and to
the reaction cells.

Rinse stations (SA/SB)
Before aspirating and after dispensing a sample, the
sample probe is rinsed inside and outside with deionized
water. The rinse station is the home position of the sample
pipetter.

Sonic wash station

Basic Wash bottle.

Status indicators

The 5 status indicators show the status of the reagent
packs in the respective loading port.

Cap pre-opener

When loading a reagent pack, the cap pre-opener opens
the reagent bottle caps to soft-close position. When
unloading a reagent pack, the cap pre-opener softly
closes the caps. Caps in soft-close position minimize
reagent evaporation.

Reagent Loader button

The Reagent Loader button calls the reagent loader or
sends it down. The LED of the button indicates the position
of the reagent loader.

Loading ports

To load a reagent pack, push it through 1 of the 5 loading
ports into the reagent loader. To unload a reagent pack,
pull it out of the reagent loader and through the
respective loading port.

Roche Diagnostics
cobas® pro integrated solutions · Software version 03-03 · User Guide · Publication version 4.2

Overview of the instrument

RFID readers

The RFID readers are mounted inside the reagent loader
shaft. For each slot in the reagent loader, there is 1 RFID
reader that reads the RFID tag on reagent packs. The RFID
tag contains the following information: The reagent pack
name, lot number, expiration date, and reagent container
code (System ID).

Reagent loader

The reagent loader transports reagent packs down to the
reagent storage level and back. Halfway down or up the
reagent loader pauses for the RFID readers to read the
RFID tags of the reagent packs.

Timer Reset button

205

To keep the reagent’s exposure to room temperature
short, the reagent loader is programmed to move down
automatically after 120 seconds. The LED of the timer
begins flashing when 30 seconds remain.
By pressing the Timer Reset button, you can extend the
loading time for 2 more minutes.

Measuring cells

The measuring cells magnetically capture the microbeads
with the attached immune complex that is to be measured.
All other serum constituents and unbound reagents in the
measuring cells are washed away with ProCell II M solution.
A photomultiplier measures the light signal that is emitted
by the ruthenium label on the immune complex under the
effect of an electrical field.

Unloading lanes

drive the main line and the return line, respectively.

Step

Progress of rack being processed

1

A rack is transported from the loading lane of the sample supply unit to the transport line.

2

The barcode reader scans the rack barcode. Then the height sensors detect the presence and type of standard
sample container. On occupied rack positions, the sample barcodes are read (barcode mode only).

3

The rack destination is determined based on test orders and the availability of the analytical unit and/or sample buffer.

4

The system transports the rack via the transport line to the sample buffer, where it waits until the analytical unit is
available for pipetting. Then the rack is transported onto the processing line of the analytical unit. If there is no rack
waiting on the sample buffer to be processed, the rack is transported directly onto the processing line of the
analytical unit.

Urgent analysis

A rack supply temporary stop may occur in the following

About rack priority
To optimize the throughput of the system and to minimize
the turnaround time of the racks on the system, the
system prioritizes the racks. The system prioritizes which
racks go to which analytical unit first, depending on how
you load your racks.

In this section
About factors for prioritizing (227)
About rack type priority (230)
About the sample pipetting sequence (231)

About factors for prioritizing

Lane position and input buffer

When a rack tray is placed, the rack transport arm
mechanism pushes all racks from the 2 loading lanes to
the transport line. The system maintains the order in which
the racks were loaded and overtaking is not possible. The
fill level of the loading lanes and the position in the rack
queue affect the loading times.

Loading location

If racks are loaded on the sample supply unit and at the
STAT port during operation, the rack in the STAT port
takes priority. Racks on the loading tray can only be
loaded when there is space to accommodate them in the
sample buffers. This does not include the slot that has
been reserved for a STAT rack. Racks on the STAT port
can only be loaded when there is space to accommodate
them in the sample buffer.

Rack type

The system prioritizes different rack types, depending on
their loading positions and if they are in an established
rack group. Examples of rack types are:
•

Routine rack

•

Calibrator rack

•

QC rack

•

(ISE v1) Wash rack

Roche Diagnostics
cobas® pro integrated solutions · Software version 03-03 · User Guide · Publication version 4.2

3 Overview of the instrument

Prioritizing by the system involves many factors. There is a
complex set of algorithms behind prioritization, which are
not covered in detail in this user documentation. An
overview of the prioritization factors is given, which are not
in order of importance.

228

About rack priority

Type of analytical unit and position from
sample supply unit

(e 801) The following statement only applies if a CC
analytical unit is part of the system configuration:
If the analytical units have the same workload, the system
gives higher priority to the immunological analytical unit.
The analytical unit which has the shortest path to the
sample supply unit takes priority for routine samples.

Current loads on the sample buffers

If the system has more than 1 sample buffer, the sample
buffer with the least workload has priority.

Current loads on the analytical units

The system prioritizes the analytical unit which would be
the fastest to complete the sampling. For this, the system
determines the analytical unit workload.

STAT rack routing

For STAT racks, the priority of analytical unit destinations
is fixed and independent from the current workload on the
individual analytical units. The STAT racks are processed in
the following order:
1. First c 503 analytical unit from the left, followed by
c 503 analytical units (if any) to the right
2. First c 703 analytical unit from the left, followed by
c 703 analytical units (if any) to the right
3. First e 801 analytical unit from the left, followed by
e 801 analytical units (if any) to the right

4. ISE analytical unit
system contains multiple analytical units of
i Ifthethesame
type, assign all STAT-relevant

applications to the first analytical unit of that type
in the system. This assignment ensures that STAT

Connection to laboratory automation system
(LAS)

Racks loaded from an LAS connection are handled as
routine racks. Those racks loaded on the sample supply
unit take priority over those coming from the LAS
connection.

Queuing system

A newly loaded rack is managed in a queuing system
depending on its priority and the priority of those racks
already on the instrument. The sequence of the queue
might change if the racks which are already on the
instrument belong to a rack group.

Overview of the instrument

229

Rack group
A rack group is formed in the following cases:
•

When more than one calibrator rack or QC rack is
loaded consecutively onto a loading tray.

•

When more than one calibrator rack or QC rack is
loaded sequentially on the STAT port within the time
range.

Samples contained in a rack group are pipetted
consecutively. A rack group which has been assigned
already cannot be overtaken, for example, by a STAT rack.
There are 3 types of rack groups:
1. Calibrator
2. QC
3. QC after calibration
A rack group is ended in the following cases:
•

When a different rack type passes the barcode
reader.

•

If there is a rack ID reading error.

•

If all racks of a loading lane are loaded.

•

If no further rack is loaded at the STAT port within the
time range (timeout).

High-priority immunology tests (e 801)

section only applies if a CC analytical unit is
i This
included in the system configuration.
Samples having strict high-priority tests ordered are
pipetted in the e 801 analytical unit first due to potential
sample carryover.
If the rack is first transported to another analytical unit
than the e 801 analytical unit:
1. All other samples on that rack are pipetted.
2. The rack is then transported to the e 801 analytical
unit and pipetted.
If the automatic rerun setting is set:
1. The rack waits on the sample buffer for the results.
2. If a rerun is required, the rack returns to the e 801
analytical unit.

Optional components
Liquid waste container
The following analytical units have separate outlets for
highly concentrated and diluted liquid waste:
•

c 503 analytical unit

•

c 703 analytical unit

•

e 801 analytical unit

The ISE analytical unit is equipped with only one outlet
through which the concentrated liquid waste is drained.
A

A Outlet for diluted
waste

B

B Outlet for highly
concentrated waste

Depending on local regulations, all outlets can be directly
connected to the drainage system.

As an option, liquid waste containers for concentrated
liquid waste are available. Each liquid waste container has
a volume of 10 L and a sensor for detecting when the
container is full. If a container is full, then the liquid waste
automatically fills into the second container. Dispose of
liquid waste according to local regulations.
u Related topics

Pre-Routine

The workflow on the Pre-Routine dialog box guides you

u About pre-routine (348)
Action is crucial. Examples: A reagent is empty, or a
maintenance action is overdue.
Action is needed. Examples: A reagent is below the defined
reagent warning level, or a calibration is required.
Loading new reagent is recommended. At least one reagent is
below the set daily requirement and the Preventive Action
check box is selected.

Overview

Displays the Overview dialog box for the following purposes:
•

To view the status and temperatures of each analytical unit

•

To enable and disable the connection to a host, to
cobas® link, or to a laboratory automation system

•

(ISE neo) To view the remaining time until ISE wash mask.

User interaction is needed.
If the incubation bath water of an analytical unit had not yet
reached 37 ± 0.1 °C when you switched the system to
Operation mode, the system has masked this analytical unit.
To enable analysis, unmask the analytical unit.

4 Overview of the user interface

Stop

Stop Sample
Supply

Stop System
Completely

The Stop Sample Supply button stops the system as
quickly as possible in an orderly procedure. Pipetted
samples are finished, and results are generated and
displayed.

Cancel

The Stop System Completely button stops the system
(emergency stop). All processes are stopped immediately,
already pipetted samples are lost. Incomplete results of
ongoing measurements are discarded and the tests need
to be repeated.

Yellow

•

Reagent is below purple reagent warning level (only

QC: Laboratory-specific target values are used
instead of manufacturer-defined values.

Blue
•

Action was successful.

•

New data are available.

Green

•

•

Analytical unit is busy (e.g., Maintenance mode,

alarms list. However, alarms are never deleted from the

About Rack Reception mode

About Rack Reception mode
The Rack Reception mode enables the system to start
the next analysis without performing preparation.
Therefore, this function can reduce the time-to-result.

Operators with administrator access rights can set the
Rack Reception function in the Menu > System > Rack
Reception dialog box.

Rack Reception

Rack Reception Mode

4

Hours

Do Not Wash Reaction Cells during Rack Reception Mode

Save

Cancel

Rack Reception mode

If the Rack Reception function is active:
•

After all current samples have been processed, the
system changes from Operation mode to Rack
Collect End and then to Rack Reception mode.
Even if the system is already in Rack Reception
mode, an analytical unit may still need some time to
complete post-operation tasks. In this status, it is not
possible to restart the system. To check the status of
an analytical unit, choose Maintenance > Monitor
Status.

4 Overview of the user interface

•

If you order further tests and start analysis during
Rack Reception mode, the system changes to
Operation mode immediately.
Even if the system is already back in Operation mode,
an analytical unit may still need some time to
complete preparation tasks. In this case, the sample
supply only starts when the analytical unit is in
Operation mode. To check the status of an analytical
unit, choose Maintenance > Monitor Status.

•

When the set period ends and all tests are completed,
the system changes to Post Operation mode and
then to Standby mode.

If the Rack Reception function is inactive:
•

Period for Rack Reception mode

The system stops Operation mode and changes to
Post Operation mode and then to Standby mode
after all current samples have been processed.

When the system mode changes to Rack Reception
mode, the set period begins (e.g., 8 h).
When you start a new run, the timer starts again with the
set period (8 h) when the system mode changes back to
Rack Reception mode.
You can set the period to 1, 2, 4, 8, 12, or 24 h.

Roche Diagnostics
cobas® pro integrated solutions · Software version 03-03 · User Guide · Publication version 4.2

Overview of the user interface

259

The Rack Reception Mode remains active until one of
the following occurs:

Do Not Wash Reaction Cells during Rack
Reception Mode

•

The set period has elapsed.

•

You clear the Rack Reception check box.

•

A red system alarm occurs.

•

You can choose Stop > Stop System Completely
or Stop > Stop Sample Supply.

This check box relates to the washing function of the
reaction cells on the CC analytical units.
If the Do Not Wash Reaction Cells during Rack
Reception Mode check box is selected:
•

After the last sample is processed, the system washes
all used reaction cells.

•

When the washing of reaction cells stops, the CC
analytical unit goes into Rack Reception mode
(check Maintenance > Monitor Status).
In this mode, you can replace the Acid Wash bottle
and the Basic Wash bottles.

•

If you start analysis again, the system washes the
reaction cells and then the system starts processing
the samples.

•

The water consumption is reduced.

•

The time-to-result could be increased.

Searching for QC values on the e-library
For each QC material lot, a Value Sheet is available.
The Value Sheet contains the QC target values and QC
ranges for all included tests and for different reagent lots,
if applicable.
When you use a new reagent lot, different QC target
values and QC ranges might apply.
For the e 801 analytical units, Value Sheets are regularly
updated and are available via the e-library. They contain
the latest assigned QC target values and QC ranges.
For the CC analytical units, the initial Value Sheets are
available via the e-library. If there are reassignments, the
Value Sheets are not updated. All reassigned QC target
values and QC ranges are listed in an Important Note for
the QC materials, which is also available via the e-library.

About cobas® c pack green – CC
System reagents are universal, assay reagents are testspecific.
•

cobas® c pack green is the reagent pack used on the
CC analytical units for assay reagents, auxiliary
reagents, and CDCs

•

Mostly ready-for-use reagent packs

•

Onboard stability of up to 6 months

•

cobas® c pack green contains 2 reagent bottles
If an application requires a third reagent, this reagent
is supplied in a separate reagent pack.

Auxiliary reagents

The following reagents are also supplied in reagent packs
and are considered as auxiliary reagents:

Roche Diagnostics
cobas® pro integrated solutions · Software version 03-03 · User Guide · Publication version 4.2

Overview of reagents and consumables

•

Special reagents: An additional reagent that is
necessary for the reaction but provided in a separate
reagent pack, can be used by multiple assays, e.g. the
START reagent.

•

Diluents: For photometric applications, either system
water or 9% NACL solution is used as diluent.

283

(c 503) For the measurement of HbA1c, the system
uses A1CD (hemolyzing reagent) as diluent.

• EcoTergent

286

About reagents and consumables – e 801

You can find this information on the Reagents > Status
menu.

Pretreatment reagents and the PT link
function

A pretreatment and an assay reagent pack form a pair to
ensure that always the same combination is used for
processing patient samples, calibrators, and QC materials.
The linkage is established during reagent registration. The
different link statuses are shown in the table below.

A pretreatment reagent pack can only form a pair with an
assay reagent pack of the same test and the same lot. This
function is called PT link.

5 Overview of reagents and consumables

A Assay reagent pack

B Pretreatment
reagent pack

Link status

Explanation

Free

The pretreatment or assay reagent pack is not yet linked to another
reagent pack. Free reagent packs are not available for
measurement.
The system tries to find a pretreatment reagent pack available for
linking.

Linked

The pretreatment or assay reagent pack is available for
measurement.
The linkage is stored at the registration time of the assay reagent
pack and/or the pretreatment reagent pack.
Once an assay reagent pack and a pretreatment reagent pack are
linked, neither can be linked to another reagent pack.

Empty

One or both of the linked reagent packs are empty.
When one of the 2 reagent packs is empty, neither of the reagent
packs can be used anymore.
The number of available tests corresponds to the lowest number of
remaining tests in one of the linked reagent packs.
Reagent packs that are not linked are empty.

y Explanation of the link statuses

About calibrators and QC materials - ISE
Calibrators are used to calibrate a reagent on a system
and QC materials are used to check the accuracy of the
system and the tests.

Calibrators

5 Overview of reagents and consumables

A

For details about calibrators, refer to the corresponding
Method Sheet.
•

Calibrators must be loaded on black calibrator racks.

•

Opened ampules should be used immediately.

•

To avoid inaccurate calibrations, remaining content
must not be stored.

•

Calibrators are loaded in standard cups or other
suitable sample containers.

•

Expired calibrators cannot be measured.

•

Up to 30 calibrators for ISE measurements can be
installed on the system.

A Calibrators for ISE measurements
QC materials

For details about QC materials, refer to the corresponding
Method Sheet.

A

•

Universal QC materials are available.

•

QC materials must be loaded on white QC racks.

•

QC materials are loaded in standard cups or other
suitable sample containers.

•

Expired QC material cannot be measured.

•

The maximum number of QC materials that can be
installed on the system is 999.

•

Ensure that patient samples, calibrators, and QC
materials are at room temperature before
measurement.

•

Due to possible evaporation effects, patient samples,
calibrators, and QC materials on board should be
measured as soon as possible.

A

A QC material for ISE and photometric tests
In general

About calibrators and QC materials - CC
Calibrators are used to calibrate a reagent on a system
and QC materials are used to check the accuracy of the
system and the tests.

For details about calibrators, refer to the corresponding
Method Sheet.
•

For tests, multi-calibrators (for example, C.f.a.s.
Proteins) and test-specific calibrators (for example,
Preciset RF) are available.

•

Calibrators must be loaded on black calibrator racks.

•

Close calibrator bottles and store them at 2-8 °C to
minimize evaporation.

•

Calibrators are loaded in standard cups or other
suitable sample containers.

•

Expired calibrators cannot be measured.

•

Up to 160 calibrators for photometric tests can be
installed on the system.

About calibrators and QC materials – e 801
Calibrators are used to calibrate a reagent on a system
and QC materials are used to check the accuracy of the
system and the tests.

Roche Diagnostics
cobas® pro integrated solutions · Software version 03-03 · User Guide · Publication version 4.2

Overview of reagents and consumables

291

Calibrators

A Green ring

For details about calibrators, refer to the corresponding
Method Sheet.

B

B Calibrator vials for
the e 801 analytical
unit

•

There are test-specific and reagent lot-specific inpack
calibrators.

•

Multi-calibrators are available and have a green ring
on the vial.

•

Calibrators must be loaded on black calibrator racks.

•

For e 801 tests, multi-calibrators and single
calibrators must be loaded on different calibrator
racks.

•

A set of single calibrators must be placed in
consecutive positions on the same rack.

•

Close calibrator vials after taking an aliquot as soon
as possible and store them at 2-8 °C to minimize
evaporation.

•

Calibrator vials must be equipped with a barcode
label. Non-barcoded calibrators must be loaded in
standard cups.

•

Expired calibrators cannot be measured.

•

Up to 100 immunology calibrators and up to
10 different calibrator lots per test can be installed on
the system.

QC materials
For details about QC materials, refer to the corresponding
Method Sheet.

A

•

QC materials must be loaded on white QC racks.

•

QC material vials are used exclusively for downloaded
Roche QC materials.

•

Expired QC materials cannot be measured.

•

The maximum number of QC materials that can be
installed on the system is 999.

•

Ensure that patient samples, calibrators, and QC
materials are at a temperature of 20-25 °C before
measurement.

•

To avoid possible evaporation, ensure that the
accumulated onboard time of the calibrators and QC
materials does not exceed the value specified in the
Method Sheet.

•

Only use specified sample containers.

A

A QC material vials for the e 801 analytical unit

Fluorinated greenhouse gas
The product contains a fluorinated greenhouse gas in the
hermetically sealed refrigeration. The insulation of the
chamber includes foam blown with fluorinated greenhouse
gas.

Environmentally friendly refrigerant

As of June 2021, the cooling units use HFO-1234yf as new
refrigerant. HFO-1234yf is considered a mildly flammable
refrigerant with relatively low burn velocity. It is much more
environmentally friendly than the one previously used.
If the safety label shown in the table is placed on the rear
side, the analytical unit uses the new refrigerant.

Noise emission
The following noise emission levels have been measured
on the respective example configuration of the system.

The maximum noise level is measured 1 m away from the
front of the system for 90 seconds. Dark noise level
(atmosphere noise) about 40 dB is contained. Intermittent
sound is excepted from the value.

control unit, at sample and reagent loading positions, and

About pre-routine

About pre-routine
To prepare the system for sample measurement, perform
all necessary tasks indicated by the colored buttons in the
Pre-Routine dialog box.
Choose the Pre-Routine button.
Pre-Routine

List
