If a button in the Pre-Routine dialog box is yellow, purple,
or red, the Pre-Routine button displays the same color. If
multiple colors are present in the Pre-Routine dialog box,
the Pre-Routine button displays the color with the
highest priority:
1. Red (highest priority)
2. Yellow
3. Purple (lowest priority)

7 Before operation

The workflow in the Pre-Routine dialog box guides you
through the pre-routine actions. You can perform some
pre-routine actions also during operation. However, the
recommended workflow is to perform these actions before
processing samples.
can configure the Pre-Routine
i Administrators
dialog box to determine what actions are included

and the sequence that they are displayed in.
Therefore, the overall number and sequence of the
displayed buttons may differ on your system.

Colors

Perform at least the actions highlighted yellow or red.

Roche Diagnostics
cobas® pro integrated solutions · Software version 03-03 · User Guide · Publication version 4.2

Before operation

349

Red: Action is crucial. Examples: A reagent is empty, or a
maintenance action is overdue.
Yellow: Action is needed. Examples: A reagent is below
the defined warning level, or a calibration is required.
Purple: Loading new reagent is recommended. At least
one reagent is below the set daily requirement and the
Preventive Action check box is selected.
Gray: No action needed.
Assumptions for pre-routine

We assume that the system uses the recommended
default settings:
•

Self-operating maintenance (the system performs
automated maintenance in the background)

•

Automatic sample management (time-triggered
backup and deletion of results)

•

Elapsed time intervals trigger a colored warning
(maintenance settings)

If your Roche Service representative has disabled some of
the default settings, you must perform the corresponding
actions manually.

Loading reagent packs – CC
If the remaining volume of a reagent pack is low, or it has
expired, load a new reagent pack.

WARNING!
Incorrect results due to bubbles or foam inside a
reagent pack
Bubbles or foam inside a reagent pack may cause
inaccurate reagent pipetting and lead to incorrect
results.
r Do not shake reagents.
r If the system detects insufficient reagent because of
foam on the surface, the system masks this reagent
pack. Remove this reagent pack briefly until the foam
disappears.

WARNING!

7 Before operation

Incorrect results due to incorrect reagent
temperature
Leaving reagent packs uncooled for a long period of time
may lead to incorrect results and influences the onboard
stability of reagents.
r During operation and maintenance, carefully follow the
instructions.
r If a reagent pack cannot be loaded, resolve the loading
issue or remove the affected reagent pack.
The reagent manager loads and unloads the reagent
packs automatically via the loading port. Reagent packs
must be loaded within 1 hour. If the reagent manager
cannot load the reagent packs within 1 hour, the system
makes them unusable for any system.

can cause deterioration in measurement accuracy.

Downloading required parameters

Downloading required parameters
To ensure accurate measurements, you must keep all
parameters up-to-date. Parameters are applications,
calibrator parameters, QC material parameters, and
special wash parameters.
The color of the Download Required Items button
indicates that parameters are available for installation:
•

Yellow: Updated parameters available, for example,
Roche has adjusted QC target values.

•

Red: Important parameters required by the system, for
example, a used lot number does not match the
installed lot number.

Lot numbers are encoded in barcode labels or RFID tags
for the reagents, calibrators, and QC materials.
all parameters listed on the Download
i Download
Required Items dialog box to ensure that the
correct parameters are available on the system.

The software displays only parameters for
download that are relevant for the current system.
For example, reagent lot-specific calibrator
parameters are only available for download if this
reagent lot has previously been loaded into the
system.

r To download parameters
1 In the Pre-Routine dialog box, choose the Download
Required Items button if it is colored.

before you process samples.

For details, refer to: Generating calibration and QC
load lists (389)

Quick reference: Pre-routine workflow

Quick reference: Pre-routine workflow
The system is intended for continuous operation (24/7). At
the beginning of a shift, log on to the system and perform
the pre-routine actions highlighted by colors in the PreRoutine dialog box.

Colors

Perform at least the actions highlighted yellow or red.
Red: Action is crucial. Examples: A reagent is empty, or a
maintenance action is overdue.
Yellow: Action is needed. Examples: A reagent is below
the defined warning level, or a calibration is required.
Purple: Loading new reagent is recommended. At least
one reagent is below the set daily requirement and the
Preventive Action check box is selected.
Gray: No action needed.
m The system or the masked analytical unit is in Standby
mode.

Ordering tests manually
The system usually receives the test orders from a
connected host. You can also order tests manually on the
control unit.
When ordering tests for samples in non-barcode mode,
note the following differences:

Routine

•

For routine samples, define a sample sequence
number. The smallest available sequence number is
prefilled.

•

For STAT samples, enter the rack ID and position on
the STAT rack. The system assigns a fixed sequence
number automatically once you save the order.

Preparing barcoded samples
In barcode mode, the system uses barcodes to identify
samples. To allow barcode scanning, place the barcode
label within the specified scan zone.

WARNING!
Incorrect results if tubes are not aligned vertically
as straight as possible and not fully inserted in the
racks.
Incorrect placement of tubes on racks may cause
incorrect pipetting, which may lead to false results,
especially when performing immunology tests.
r Ensure that tubes and cups are always placed
vertically as straight as possible and are inserted fully
in the racks.
r Only use tubes specified for the use with the system.

d

m Rack trays
m Barcode labels
m Sample containers
m Sample racks, with rack IDs according to the rack
assignment for the sample type and container type
u About choosing the correct sample container and rack
range (116)

r To prepare barcoded samples

2 Use suitable racks:
• The rack ID must be according to the rack
assignment for the sample type and container type.
• Use tube adapters for tubes with an outer diameter
of 13 mm or less.

Preparing samples in non-barcode mode
In non-barcode mode, the system identifies samples only
by their sequence on the racks. You must organize the
sequence of the samples manually or with your host to
track the samples’ identities.

WARNING!
Incorrect results due to a sample mismatch
Putting a sample container on a wrong position may lead
to incorrect results.

r Take care when you work in non-barcode mode
because of the risk of sample mismatch.
r Do not exchange or remove samples.

ordered in.

Loading samples onto the loading lane
After preparing the samples in containers, load the rack
trays onto the loading lane. You can load additional
samples at any time, even during operation.
m The system is operating or in Standby mode.
m Tests have been ordered at the host or manually at the
control unit.

r To load samples
1 Slide the racks onto a rack tray. In non-barcode mode,
strictly follow the order given in the Test Order List.
I Ensure that the slit in the bottom of the rack is slid
correctly into the guide rail of the rack tray.
If the rack is incorrectly placed on top of the guide
rail, it might fall over during the loading process.

Roche Diagnostics
cobas® pro integrated solutions · Software version 03-03 · User Guide · Publication version 4.2

8 During operation

j

420

Running patient samples

2 Move the racks to the front of the tray, so that there is
no gap between the individual racks.

3 Ensure that the status indicators are lit.
I If necessary, wait for the sample supply unit to
process rack trays that have already been loaded.
The status indicators will turn on after the other
rack trays have been processed.
4 Open the main cover of the sample supply unit.

5 Load the prepared rack trays with the handle at the
right side.
f If the system is in Operation mode, it processes
the samples without any further action.
6 If the system is not already in Operation mode,
choose the Start button and start the run.

analytical units are in Operation mode. To check
the status of an analytical unit, select

f The system performs several function checks. The
software generates an alarm, for example, when
system reagents are unavailable.
f After the system has entered Operation mode, the
sample processing begins.

Ordered
Sample has not been pipetted yet or an open order exists (e.g.,
automatic rerun due to data alarm).
Processing
Sample is being processed.
Complete
Results are available. No data alarm occurred.
Incomplete
Test was masked or data alarm occurred.
Results for this sample have been uploaded to Host.

8 During operation

Additional tests for samples marked by #

•

ISE analytical unit

•

CC analytical unit

The # indicates that this sample is potentially affected by
sample carryover because of the previous pipetting out of
this sample container without special wash.
•

For additionally ordered tests which would have
required a special wash before the first pipetting, the
Samp.O data alarm is attached to the result. Repeat
the test with a newly aliquoted sample.

•

If an HPI test has been measured in an additional run
on a sample with # status, the Samp.O data alarm is
also attached to that result. Repeat the test with a
newly aliquoted sample.

Identifying the expected result time
For each sample, you can view the expected time when the
results are available. The system calculates the time after
all tests have been pipetted.
For cobas® e flow tests, the system cannot calculate the
expected result time because the number of embedded
tests to be requested depend on the subresults. Thus, no
expected result time is displayed for samples with a
cobas® e flow test.

About processing additional samples during a run
Automatic sample supply in barcode mode

When the system is operating, it automatically processes
newly loaded rack trays and racks loaded via the STAT
port during the current run. You do not need to start
another run.

•

Load a rack via the STAT port.

•

When the status indicators are lit:
– Load a new rack tray.
– Lift the handle of a rack tray in the loading area
briefly (restart trigger).

The system is operating refers to the following modes:
•

Operation

•

Rack Reception

•

Rack Supply Complete

•

Rack Collect End

428

Prioritizing a sample

Prioritizing a sample
For urgently needed results, you can increase the
processing priority of a routine sample.
To shorten the turnaround time, the rack with the selected
sample is processed with STAT priority. However, the rack
type and visible sample priority (routine) remains
unchanged.
Racks supplied via the STAT port are already processed
with STAT priority. You cannot increase their priority.
Changing the priority is also not possible for calibrator
racks and QC racks.

j

m The system is in Operation mode.
m The rack is a routine rack or rerun rack.

r To change the priority of a sample
1 Choose Routine > Results.
2 Choose the sample to be processed with STAT priority.
3 From the options menu , choose the Change Priority
button.
4 Choose the Confirm button.

prioritized rack are highlighted in red.

• If the field is empty, no special wash rule for the

Some cobas® e flow tests use calculated embedded tests
in addition to measured embedded tests.
For such cobas® e flow tests, the numerical values of the
measured subresults are not relevant for the calculation
and are displayed with asterisks in the Result column.
Only the calculated subresults show a numerical value
whereas only the measured subresults contain reagent
information.
subresults can only be evaluated
i Calculated
together with the main result or the corresponding

measured subresult. If a data alarm is attached to
a measured subresult, the alarm is not applied to a
connected calculated subresult. However the main
result gets an eflowE data alarm in this case.

8 During operation

Exception: The data alarms QCErr and HU on a
subresult do not trigger an eflowE data alarm on
the main result.

Unloading a sample ahead of schedule
If you need the sample before regular processing is
completed, you can unload the rack manually. However,
you cannot unload calibrator racks and QC racks
manually.
The system keeps the remaining test orders as open
orders. After you have reloaded the sample, the system
measures the remaining open test orders.

Loading reagents during operation
When the system operates 24/7, pre-routine is not
necessarily done at the beginning of a shift. You can also
replace most reagents and consumables during operation.
During operation, however, reagent loading might be
slower than in Standby mode.

Reagent Management List

This report displays the reagent needs based on set
reagent warning levels. It also displays expired reagents.
In the Total on Board column, the number in brackets
indicates the level set as the daily requirement (purple
warning).
In the Expiry Date column, the number in brackets
indicates the remaining onboard stability or shelf life in
days, depending on which elapses first.

8 During operation

To use this report effectively, your administrator must set
appropriate reagent warning levels (purple and yellow) for
each reagent.

Consumption-Based Load List

This report displays the reagent needs per weekday based
on the actual usage per business day for the last 9 weeks.
This report is helpful when the number of tests varies
between the weekdays, for example, because the
laboratory performs certain tests only on certain
weekdays.
The columns have the following meanings:
•

Average consumption: Mean consumption of this
reagent in the last 9 weeks on the current weekday

•

Safety margin: 10% of the average consumption

•

Total: Sum of average consumption and safety margin
(10%)

Manually masking and unmasking reagent packs, tests, and analytical units

Manually masking and unmasking reagent
packs, tests, and analytical units
Masked reagent packs, tests, or analytical units are
unavailable to measure samples.
In addition to this manual masking, the system can
automatically mask the following when, for example, they
are empty or have expired:
•

Reagent packs

•

System reagents

•

ISE reagents

•

ISE electrodes

On Routine > Order Tests, you can check whether a test
is masked for some reason:
User Mask
Something required for this test is currently masked:
•

test mask or patient mask

•

unit masked

•

reagent pack patient mask

Assay Reagent Mask
The system has masked the test because a reagent is
empty or has expired.
Other Reagent Mask

8 During operation

The system has masked the test because the following
reagent is missing:
•

ISE mask as washing is required

•

ISE electrode mask (expired or remaining test is zero)

•

Diluent: only for tests using a predilution

•

Special reagent (CC only)

•

Cleaner: If both tests, victim and offender, of a
defined special wash are loaded on the same reagent
disk, the victim test is masked.

•

(e 801) PreClean II M

Calib. Mask
The system has masked a reagent because it has no valid
calibration or the last calibration failed (automatic
calibration mask).
QC Mask
The system has masked a reagent due to its QC status
(automatic reagent patient mask by QC).

Masking and unmasking reagent packs
Mask a reagent pack to make it temporarily unavailable for
sample processing. The system starts using a standby
reagent pack if available.
Reagent pack mask

Mask a reagent pack, for example, in the following cases:
•

If you do not perform a specific test, you can mask the
reagent pack for this time.

•

If there is a failure and you cannot troubleshoot at the
moment, you can mask the reagent pack and use the
standby reagent pack.

system can still use a manually masked
i The
reagent pack for calibration and QC measurement.
You can mask assay reagent packs but not the following:
•

Diluents

•

(CC) Wash solutions

•

(CC) Special reagents

•

(e 801) Pretreatments

8 During operation

(e 801) If a reagent pack is part of a linked kit or linked
test, the linked reagent pack is also masked.

Masking and unmasking tests
The system excludes masked tests from measurement.
This saves time and QC material, for example, when you do
not use certain tests on certain days.
You can mask tests for samples only (Patient Mask) or for
all tests including calibration and QC (Test Mask).
You can mask every ISE test separately.
(e 801) You can mask tests on both measuring channels
separately.
Exception: For cobas® e flow tests, the system always
masks both measuring channels collectively.

Ordering calibrations
The software recommends calibrations according to the
intervals set for each application. You only have to order
the recommended calibrations.
To ensure accuracy, you must perform a QC measurement
after calibrating a test.
QC after calibration function

If you load the QC racks directly after the calibrator racks
in the same run, the system will measure QC automatically
after calibrating the tests. You do not need to order a QC.
Note: The tests must be activated for the QC material.
after calibration does not work for additional
i QC
applications where the calibration data is copied

(copy calibration). QC after calibration works only
with the primary application. For additional ACNs,
you must reload the QC rack.

About stopping the system
The system provides 3 methods for stopping operation,
which differ in urgency.

Emergency stop

To stop operation immediately, choose Stop > Stop
System Completely. The system stops processing at
the end of the current mechanical cycle. Pipetting and all
measurements are stopped. When resuming operation,
perform Maintenance > 2 Reset Transport Lines to
unload racks.

Sampling stop

To stop the sample supply unit from loading new racks,
choose Stop > Stop Sample Supply. The system
continues to process all pipetted tests until results are
available and then enters Standby mode.

Stop after current run

Emergency stop

To put the system to Standby mode when all samples are
processed, clear the Rack Reception Mode check box in
the Start dialog box.

Sampling stop

completed

If quick start mode is enabled, finalization is only performed partly.

Quick start mode - e 801

Quick start mode is an operating mode of the e 801
analytical unit. It is similar to the Standby mode but it
allows for a much quicker return to Operation.
the quick start mode is active, the ECL sipper
i Ifflow
paths and the ProCell/CleanCell cups are not

filled with water during Post Operation. Not filling
with water may lead to crystallization after long
idle time. Therefore, perform Maintenance > 31
Finalization if the system stopped and you do not
restart operation.

Unloading samples

The workflow above illustrates batch processing.
Alternatively, the system can be set up for real-time
processing. With real-time processing, the first 2 steps
change: You merely load samples and the system
automatically fetches the corresponding orders from the
host.
Real-time processing is a handshake protocol between
host and control unit. The protocol includes all messages
from the detection of the rack to the output of the result.
Batch processing is unidirectional. Messages like test
orders or test results are sent either from the control unit
to the host or vice versa, regardless of the system status.

About pipetting volumes and dilution factors
You can perform tests with selectable dilution factors (i.e.,
1:3, 1:20, etc.), with normal, decreased, or increased
pipetting volumes, or with a manual dilution, depending on
the application.

Application of pipetting volumes and dilution
factors

There are different ways pipetting volumes and dilution
factors can be applied:
•

Pipetting volumes and dilution factors are
programmed in the application file.

•

ISE: Only the pipetting volumes programmed in the
application file are applied.

•

You can manually select a dilution or one of the 3
levels of normal, decreased, or increased pipetting
volumes, depending on the application.

•

The host can order predefined pipetting volumes and
dilution factors.

10 Non-routine operation

Manual dilution

Manually diluted samples are samples that you have
diluted before you load the samples onto the system.
Manual dilution should not be confused with manually
selected dilution factors. Manually selected dilution
factors are applied by the system and considered
automatically for the calculation of the result.
In contrast, the dilution factor of a manual dilution is not
considered automatically for the calculation of the final
result. On the report, results for manually diluted samples
are indicated by Manually diluted. On Routine > Results
> Test Review, there is a mark in the Dil. column.
It is your responsibility to calculate the final result for
manually diluted samples.

About the sample index measurement
To ensure accurate measurement of samples, you can
order sample index values for lipemia (L), hemolysis (H),
and icterus (I) together with any test order on CC
analytical units.

Sample index values

Lipemia, hemolysis, and icterus can interfere with the
measurement of samples. The sample index values are
used to indicate this interference.
Sample index values

of interference

y Sample index values

Sample Index Limits

Each application has specific interference limits. Refer to
the corresponding Method Sheet.

(ISE) The Sample Index Limits area is displayed on Menu
> Application > Reference Ranges.
If a sample index value of a patient sample is above the
application-specific interference limit, the condition of the
sample causes measurement interference and a data
alarm is issued. The data alarm indicates that this test
result deviates by at least 10%.
In all application settings, the sample index limits for L, H,
and I are implemented in conventional measurement units.

About automatic rerun tests

Prerequisites for automatic rerun

To enable the execution of automatic reruns for a test, the
following settings must be activated:
1. For all tests: Start > Retain Rack in System for
Automatic Rerun
2. For the respective test: Menu > Application >
Analytical Parameters
If both settings are active, the sample remains on the
system until the first result for this test is available. This
enables the system to perform a rerun test automatically
without reloading the sample, if necessary.
Automatic rerun functionality does not apply for HbA1c
applications.
off automatic rerun test for qualitative
i Switch
immunology tests.

Roche Diagnostics
cobas® pro integrated solutions · Software version 03-03 · User Guide · Publication version 4.2

10 Non-routine operation

If automatic rerun is activated system-wide and
application-specific for at least 1 ordered test, the sample
remains on the sample buffer until the results of the
sample are available. If a data alarm specified to trigger an
automatic rerun test is attached to a test result, this
sample is automatically measured again in the same run.

data alarms. For the data alarms that can trigger an
automatic rerun test, see the list of data alarms that
generate an automatic rerun test.

Automatic rerun for HPI tests

section only applies if a CC analytical unit is
i This
included in the system configuration.
For high-priority immunology tests (HPI), the system
distinguishes between strict and non-strict HPI tests:

Strict HPI tests

If an order includes strict HPI tests, the sample is always
processed first on an e 801 analytical unit before it is
processed on any other analytical unit.
To avoid the deviation of test results between a first run
and a rerun caused by sample carryover, the system
behaves as follows: Only when all immunology tests,

Roche Diagnostics
cobas® pro integrated solutions · Software version 03-03 · User Guide · Publication version 4.2

Non-routine operation

497

including potential reruns, have been completed on an
e 801 analytical unit, the sample with strict HPI orders
goes to other analytical units.

Non-strict HPI tests

If an order includes a non-strict HPI test, special washes
are applied. The sample can be processed first on any
analytical unit.
Whenever the sample reaches an analytical unit other than
the e 801, the sample probe is washed with ultrasound
before the pipetting is started. For that reason, the
sample does not have to wait for potential reruns on an
e 801 analytical unit.

Repeating a test by setting up repeat limits
To double-check results within a clinically relevant
concentration range, you can set a lower and upper
repeat limit for each test.
If the result is outside the repeat limit but inside the
technical limit, the test is repeated using the same sample
pipetting volume as in the first run. In Menu > System >
Alarms, you can activate the automatic rerun in case of a
repeat limit data alarm.

About strict and non-strict high-priority immunology
tests (HPI)
Immunology applications that are sensitive to sample
carryover are defined as high-priority immunology tests
(HPI tests).
section only applies if a CC analytical unit is
i This
included in the system configuration.
The e 801 analytical unit uses tips but other analytical
units use durable sample probes for pipetting.
Thus, HPI tests must only be considered for systems
combining an e 801 analytical unit with other AU types.

Identification of HPI tests on the user
interface

On cobas® pro integrated solutions, there are 2 types of
high-priority tests (HPI):
•

Strict HPI tests: Immunology tests which are sensitive
for sample carryover. Therefore, the sample is always
processed on the e 801 analytical unit first.

•

Non-strict HPI tests: Immunology tests that can use
ultrasonic washing to avoid relevant sample carryover.
Therefore, the sample can be processed first on any
analytical unit. When the sample reaches an analytical
unit different than the e 801 analytical unit, the
sample probe is always washed with ultrasound before
the first sampling.

You cannot distinguish strict and non-strict HPI tests on
Menu > Application.
Instead, choose Menu > Special Wash > Sample Probe.
In the Manufacturer Rules table:
•

Non-strict HPI tests: e 801 tests having an entry
including a Washing Method for another AU.

•

Strict HPI tests: e 801 tests having an entry without a
Washing Method for another AU.

• Running patient samples (411)
• Checking test results (429)

Non-barcode mode (sequence mode)
The system uses an internal worklist to track the sequence
of samples. On the worklist, samples are sequentially
numbered and assigned to racks by rack ID and rack
position.

The Test Order List on Report > Routine represents
the internal worklist.
In non-barcode mode, the system uses only the sample
sequence number to identify samples. Optionally, you can
still assign a sample ID, which can be text, to help identify
samples.

Switching between barcode mode and non‑barcode mode
Before switching from barcode mode to non-barcode
mode or vice versa, you must delete all samples from the
system.
First, archive all sample records.
u Saving and backing up data (613)
Then you must determine if the samples must be deleted
from the host as well.
deleting samples from the host, refer to the
i For
respective User Guide.
In barcode mode, the sample ID is used to identify each
sample. The barcode on a sample container represents
the sample ID. Each sample is included in the sample
databases of the system and of the host. Therefore, you
cannot easily switch between barcode mode and nonbarcode mode without risking duplicate sample IDs in one
of the databases.

About starting a run in non-barcode mode
When you start a run in non-barcode mode, the system
automatically sets the starting sample number. The
starting sample number is the number of the first sample
of the run. Depending on the previous run, you might have
to adjust the starting sample number.
The system always increments the starting sample number
by 5.

In the case of fewer than 5 samples

105

103

109

...

106 = 103

For example, if the last rack of the previous run has
2 samples with the sample numbers 101 and 102 on
positions 1 and 2, the first sample of the new run has the
sample number 103.

...

In the case of a full rack

However, the system sets the starting sample number of
the new run automatically to 106. In this case, you have to
adjust the starting sample number from 106 to 103.

If the last rack of the previous run has no empty positions,
the starting sample number that the system sets
automatically is correct. In this case, you do not need to
adjust the starting sample number.

Expiration date (shelf life)

The shelf life ends with the expiration date which is defined
by the manufacturer. Never use materials past the
expiration date.

Mask expired reagents and electrodes

WARNING!
Incorrect results when using expired reagents
Data collected using expired reagents is not reliable.
r Do not use reagents that have exceeded their
expiration date or onboard stability, otherwise you may
obtain inaccurate data.
If you check the Mask Expired Reagents and
Electrodes box under Menu > System > Analyzer, you
cannot use the following since they are masked
automatically when they expire (shelf life):
•

Reagents

•

ISE electrodes

Roche Diagnostics
cobas® pro integrated solutions · Software version 03-03 · User Guide · Publication version 4.2

Non-routine operation

517

If you clear the check box, expired reagents are not
masked, but the results are flagged with a ReagEx data
alarm.
The Mask Expired Reagents and Electrodes check box
applies to the following items on expiry:
•

ISE reagents and ISE electrodes

•

Assay reagents

•

Linked pretreatment reagents

Development channels can be used to create applications
from other companies to use on the cobas® pro
integrated solutions. The user can create the application
on a Roche web portal. These applications can then be
sent to cobas® link and downloaded onto the system
software in the usual way as is done with a standard
application.

Cap pre-opener

527

When loading a reagent pack, the cap pre-opener opens
the bottle caps to soft-close position. Caps in soft-close
position minimize reagent evaporation.
When unloading a reagent pack, the cap pre-opener
cannot fully close the caps. If you want to store unloaded
reagent packs for later use, fully close the caps manually.

About cobas® e flow tests - e 801
The cobas® e flows are combinations of embedded tests
in a predefined testing process on the e 801 analytical
unit. Depending on primary results cobas® pro can
automatically order rerun tests with a different dilution,
repeat tests, or reflex tests. By this, cobas® e flow tests
allow automated performance of previously manual steps
as well as the calculation of a main result based on
different sub-results.
Since previously manual steps are automated within the
cobas® e flow tests, turnaround times are optimized and
errors are reduced.
Examples of cobas® e flow tests:
•

HIV Duo (2 embedded tests, AHIV, HIV Ag)

•

CMV lgG Avidity (pretreatment of sample aliquot)

•

Anti-HCV II R (1 embedded test, duplicate repeat test
without dilution if first test result is Initially reactive)

•

HBsAg II quant II (2 embedded tests, automated rerun
test with 3-step dilution)

How a cobas® e flow test works

A cobas® e flow test is ordered manually on the system or
via a connected host system. If ordered, the
corresponding sequence of embedded tests is performed
automatically. The results of the measured embedded
tests are collected, processed and validated within the
system, so that the cobas® e flow main result can be
produced according to the cobas® e flow design. The
cobas® e flow main result together with all defined
subresults including flags and alarms if available, is
forwarded to the connected host system according to the
design of the cobas® e flow test.
Similar to normal tests, Roche provides application
parameter files for cobas® e flow tests. There are no lot
specific parameters available for cobas® e flow tests.
e flow embedded tests must be calibrated
i cobas®
outside of the cobas® e flow test. Calibration and

QC are not performed as part of the cobas® e flow
test.

Embedded tests

529

The immunology tests that are performed on the e 801
analytical unit as part of cobas® e flow tests are called
embedded tests. The operator cannot order embedded
tests separately.
There are 2 types of embedded tests:
1. Embedded tests can be identical copies of a regular
test using the same reagent pack but having another
ACN for example, AHCV2.
2. For certain embedded tests, there is no
corresponding regular test available, for example
AHIV or HIV Ag.
It is not possible to process such an embedded test
without cobas® e flow
u Setting up a cobas® e flow test (1148)

Linked tests for cobas® e flow tests

Some embedded tests that are performed as part of
cobas® e flow tests use the same reagent pack. These
tests are called linked tests. Linked tests are pipetted in a
strict sequence. If there is a failure of one linked test, all
linked tests are repeated.

Linked kits for cobas® e flow duo tests

Linked kits refer to cobas® e flow duo tests. Linked kits are
unrelated to linked tests.
The applications and reagent packs of the involved
embedded tests are linked on the e 801 analytical unit.
Reagent packs that are to be linked come in one pack and
have the same lot number.

failure of one test, all tests must be repeated with the
same pipetting sequence.

About multi-application tests - e 801
Multi-application tests use the same reagent pack, but
with different measurement protocols from different
applications.

10 Non-routine operation

General concept of multi-application tests

One typical deployment is the measurement of one
parameter for 2 purposes:
•

Measurement with a regular measurement protocol
for routine samples

•

Measurement with an accelerated measurement
protocol for STAT samples

However, the tests that are part of one multi-application
test can be ordered independently and are performed
independently.
Up to 4 applications can be part of 1 multi-application
test. The different applications have individual application
code numbers.

Reagent status information

Individual calibration and QC are necessary because of
the different measurement protocols.

About pretreatment reagents and the PT link function - e 801
A pretreatment and an assay reagent pack form a pair to
ensure that always the same combination is used for
calibration, QC and sample measurement. The linkage is
established during reagent registration. The different link
statuses are shown in the table below.

B

A

B Pretreatment
reagent pack

Link status

Explanation

Free

The pretreatment or assay reagent pack is not yet linked to another
reagent pack. Free reagent packs are not available for
measurement.
The system tries to find a pretreatment reagent pack available for
linking.

Linked

The pretreatment or assay reagent pack is available for
measurement.
The linkage is stored at the registration time of the assay reagent
pack and/or the pretreatment reagent pack.
Once an assay reagent pack and a pretreatment reagent pack are
linked, neither can be linked to another reagent pack.

y Explanation of the link statuses

A Assay reagent pack

A pretreatment reagent pack can only form a pair with an
assay reagent pack of the same test and the same lot. This
function is called PT link.

Explanation

One or both of the linked reagent packs are empty.
When one of the 2 reagent packs is empty, neither reagent packs
can be used anymore.

remaining tests in one of the linked reagent packs.
Reagent packs that are not linked are empty.

Quick reference: cobas® e flow HIV Duo
A cobas® e flow duo test is an independent measurement
of one parameter using different tests: HIV Ag and antiHIV.
Each test will be calibrated separately. Based on the
respective calibration, the ratio of signal/cutoff (i.e., the
cutoff index, COI) will be calculated when measuring
samples.
The tests HIV Ag and anti-HIV can only be ordered
together as HIV Duo cobas® e flow test. After
measurement, the system calculates a common HIV Duo
result based on the HIV Ag and anti-HIV single test results.

About calibration
The purpose of calibration is to assure accurate
measurements for all tests. Each test is calibrated to
determine a valid calibration factor. The measured values
depend on the measuring system and the reagents and
may deviate over time. Therefore, it is necessary to repeat
calibrations regularly. However, the system provides high
calibration stability to permit long calibration intervals.

In this section
What is calibration? (539)
About lot and reagent pack calibration (540)
About copy calibration (546)
About verifying calibration results (547)

What is calibration?
Calibration is specific to each analytical unit, measuring
unit, measuring channel, and reagent.

Calibration

Automatic

Manual

The system automatically recommends tests that must be
calibrated. To ensure uninterrupted operation, you must
perform this recommended calibration before starting
operation. Additionally, the host can send an order for
calibration or you can order individual tests for manual
calibration.

540

Calibration

Recommended calibration

If a test requires calibration, the system automatically
recommends calibrating this test. Before starting
operation, you must order all recommended tests for
calibration. Depending on the specified calibration
interval, you may also need to calibrate recommended
tests during operation.
u About calibration causes (565)

Manual calibration

If you decide to perform a manual calibration, individually
select the tests to be calibrated in Calibration > Order.
u Performing calibration (453)

Calibration results

When the set calibration quality criteria are met, the
calibration is considered successful. Otherwise, the
calibration has failed.
The system checks each calibration automatically. If the
calibration was successful, the calibrated tests are valid
and the system continues operation. If the system detects
an irregular condition or result, an alarm is issued and the
calibration is classified as failed and recommended to be
repeated.
You can check the results in Routine > Recent
Calibrations, in Calibration > Results, or the
corresponding print reports.

10 Non-routine operation

Calibration masking

If no valid calibration is available for a test, calibration
masking ensures that this test is not performed.
The test can be masked separately for each particular
analytical unit.

About lot and reagent pack calibration
Each reagent pack used for measuring must have a valid
calibration. The calibration parameters can be valid for a
particular reagent pack (reagent pack calibration) or for
an entire lot (lot calibration).
Roche Diagnostics
cobas® pro integrated solutions · Software version 03-03 · User Guide · Publication version 4.2

Non-routine operation

541

When you use a new reagent pack, the system checks the
calibration status. If a valid lot calibration exists, the
reagent pack is used for measurements by applying the lot
calibration factor. If not, the reagent pack must be
calibrated. Depending on how long the reagent pack is
already on the system at the time of calibration, the
calibration can become valid as a lot calibration or as a
reagent pack calibration.

About calibration masking
Calibration masking is an optional function which prevents
the processing of a test in case the corresponding reagent
in use (Status: Current) has no valid calibration at all or
the last calibration failed.

ISE calibrations

An ISE calibration is only valid for 24 hours. After
expiration, the ISE tests are masked, regardless of the
settings.
On Calibration > Order, a timer in the Cause column
indicates for how long the current ISE calibration remains
valid. When the timer elapses, the system masks the ISE
tests until you generate a valid ISE calibration.

You must calibrate the corresponding test. When the test
has been calibrated successfully, the system unmasks the
test automatically.

Setting up calibration masking and behavior
of the system

Administrators can disable automatic calibration masking
by a system-wide and a test-specific setting.
If both settings are activated, calibration masking is
enabled. The reagents are then masked for sample and QC
measurement. In case a calibration is currently being
processed, the masking becomes effective after the
calibration is finished and failed.
If one of the settings is deactivated, automatic masking is
disabled. Whether the system performs a test with no valid
calibration or not, depends on the circumstances (refer to
the right section of the diagram).
If there was a previous valid calibration, the system
calculates the result based on the last valid calibration.

Diagram for calibration masking

The system behavior depends on the settings and the
availability of previous calibration parameters as shown in
the following diagram.
Calibration masking is done in the following cases:
•

There is no valid calibration at all.

•

A calibration was performed and failed.

•

The ISE calibration was invalidated based on timeout.

•

There is an open reagent pack changeover
recommendation.

Rejecting failed calibrations

545

When a calibration becomes invalid or fails, the system
recommends a calibration. The corresponding calibration
cause is displayed on Calibration > Order.
Rejecting a failed calibration allows the system to ignore
the failed calibration and to use the last valid calibration
to calculate the sample and QC results.
If you reject a failed calibration, the cause (Failed) is
deleted. However, the previously displayed
recommendation (e.g., Timeout) remains until you
recalibrate the test successfully.
For ISE tests, rejecting failed calibrations is not available.
The ISE calibration becomes invalid and has to be
recalibrated.
when a calibration failed, a related QC after
i Even
calibration is processed, i.e. the QC material is
pipetted and measured.

If automatic calibration masking is enabled and calibration
becomes invalid or fails, the system behaves as follows:
•

If samples or QC measurements are processed while
the failing calibration is still being performed, the
Cal.E alarm is attached to results.

•

After the calibration failed, the test is masked and no
samples are pipetted for this test (B).

•

If a calibration is invalid (A), a test is also masked and
therefore not pipetted.

•

If calibration fails and a previous valid calibration is
available, you can reject the failed calibration on the
following analytical units:
– CC analytical units
– e 801 analytical unit
In this case, the result is calculated with the last valid
calibration and no Cal.E alarm is attached (C).

Details if tests are not masked

If automatic calibration masking is disabled and calibration
becomes invalid or fails, the system behaves as follows:
•

If a former valid calibration exists, this calibration is
used for calculating the result. The Cal.E alarm is
attached to all sample and QC results (D).

•

If you reject the failed calibration, the result is
calculated with the last valid calibration and no Cal.E
alarm is attached to the results (C).

About AutoCal for ISE
AutoCal for ISE is an optional function on the ISE neo
analytical unit to generate new calibration parameter after
replacement of the ISE Internal Standard reagent bottle
based on a valid ISE calibration. The AutoCal for ISE does
not require any calibrator material.

•

The function is activated in the system settings.

•

Only the ISE Internal Standard bottle is replaced.

•

The last generated ISE calibration is still valid.

After ordering the recommended AutoCal for ISE, during
the next Preparation mode the system performs the
following automatically:
•

Reagent prime and measurement of the IS EMF.

•

Recalculation of the IS concentration based on the IS
EMF values before and after bottle replacement.

If the AutoCal for ISE fails, an ISE calibration is required.
If the AutoCal for ISE is successful, the ISE analytical unit
is ready for QC and sample processing using the new ISE
Internal Standard bottle.

About loading calibrators - CC
To ensure that calibration is performed, you must follow
certain rules when loading the calibrators. There are
different rules for the different analytical units.

Multi-calibrator

•

Use black calibrator racks.

•

Use separate racks for barcoded and non-barcoded
calibrators.

•

Use standard containers as calibrator containers.

•

Do not use micro cups as calibrator containers.

•

You can mix standard containers on a calibrator rack.

You can use a multi-calibrator to calibrate multiple
applications.

About downloaded K-factor
A K-factor is used in the calculation of sample results. Any
test that requires more than a blank value during
calibration has its K-factor calculated by the measured
absorbance values of the calibrator 1 and the other
calibrators.
Photometric tests with a calibration type Linear Slope can
use a fixed, downloaded K-factor. The respective tests
update their blank values during calibration. The
application fixes the downloaded K-factor and generates a
calibration curve in combination with the absorbance
obtained only by measuring low concentration S1.
When the system detects any abnormalities during a
parameter check, the system issues a system alarm.

About AutoCal for CC (automatic lot change calibration)

Automatic lot change calibration applies to specific tests
for CC analytical units.
For these tests the AutoCal method is displayed in the
Changeover Settings area on Menu > Application >
Calibration.

calibration curve for this reagent lot can be calculated
without a new calibration measurement. The calculation is

About calibration - e 801
To assure accurate measuring, all immunology tests must
have a valid calibration.

In this section
About calibration of immunology tests (556)
About single and multi-calibrators (557)

About calibration of immunology tests

10 Non-routine operation

On the e 801 analytical unit, an individual test of a reagent
pack has a valid calibration when the test is calibrated
successfully or the valid calibration is copied from the
corresponding primary application (copy calibration).
A reagent pack on the e 801 analytical unit can have up to
4 different ACNs corresponding to up to 4 different tests.
A test can be a single test or a test embedded in a testing
process (cobas® e flow test).

cobas® e flow tests

A cobas® e flow test combines several embedded tests in
a defined testing process. All embedded tests must have a
valid calibration. They must be calibrated individually. Or, if
embedded tests are identical copies of their regular-test
counterparts, they use the same reagent pack and the
same measurement protocol. Then, there is no need for
individual calibration of an embedded test. The calibration
curve of a so-called primary application is copied to up to
3 so-called additional applications (embedded tests). You
cannot calibrate a cobas® e flow test as a whole.

Calibrators

Calibrators for the e 801 analytical unit are single or multicalibrators:
•

A single calibrator is used for one specific ACN.

•

A multi-calibrator is used for multiple ACNs.

Roche Diagnostics
cobas® pro integrated solutions · Software version 03-03 · User Guide · Publication version 4.2

Non-routine operation

557

You can install up to 100 calibrators and up to 10 different
lots per test. To install a calibrator, you must download
the calibrator parameters via cobas® link.
The system counts the number of calibrations for which a
calibrator is specified. Barcoded calibrator vials for
immunology tests can be used to calibrate a maximum of 4
measuring cells.
There are 2 types of calibrators:
•

Calibrators that come in vials and are ready for use.

•

Lyophilized calibrators that must be prepared
according to the Method Sheet and transferred to a
sample container.

For immunology tests, routine and inpack calibrators are
used:

Calibrator set

•

The calibrator code is used to identify routine
calibrators. The lot numbers of the calibrator and
reagent pack must not correspond.

•

Inpack calibrators are delivered within the reagent
package. Calibrator code and lot number are used for
identification. The lot number of the calibrator and
reagent pack must correspond.

A calibrator set includes all calibrators necessary for one
immunology test. A calibrator set may be single calibrators
or multi-calibrators. Single and multi-calibrators cannot be
mixed in one calibrator set.
u Related topics
• About types of cobas® e flow tests - e 801 (529)

About calibration causes
The system automatically recommends all tests that
require calibration. The tests recommended by the system
must be calibrated to ensure that the analytical unit
measures accurately.

Failed

Timeout

QC Violation

Calib. Now

Update

If the Calibration indicator turns yellow, calibration of
one or more tests is recommended. You must order these
tests for calibration before starting operation, or as soon
as it fits into your operation workflow. Calibration is
performed for these tests with a preset calibration
method. Calibration and QC must be completed
successfully before operation.

Calibration

Color coding of the Cause column

Under Calibration > Order, the meaning of the colors in
the Cause column is as follows:
No color
Calibration is neither recommended nor ordered for this
test.
Yellow
The system recommends this test for calibration.
Light green
Calibration is ordered for the next run.

u Setting up system recommendations for calibration

QC Violation

QC violation is the function for managing the accuracy of a
calibration by the QC result. The QC violation judges
whether the result of the QC measurement is within the
limits specified in the application. If the result of the QC
measurement is outside the range, the system
recommends calibration for the test.
u Setting up system recommendations for calibration
(568)

Calib. Now

If the Activate "Calib. Now" Cause check box is
selected (Menu > System > Calibration and QC) and a
calibration is due within the time set in Calibration >
Order in the Calib-now Timer field, you can perform
calibration in advance. This calibration ensures that you do
not have to interrupt the operation for calibrating due
tests.
u Setting up the Calib. Now settings (569)

Update (CC only)

If you download updated calibration parameters, you must
perform a calibration for all the affected reagent packs on
board.

The last calibration measurement for this reagent

Setting up the Calib. Now settings

If a calibration is due within the time defined on
Calibration > Order in the Calib-now Timer field, you
can perform calibration in advance. This calibration
ensures that you do not have to interrupt the operation for
calibrating tests with overdue calibrations.
Calib. Now for ISE tests

If the Activate "Calib. Now" Cause check box is
selected, at the latest 2 hours before the ISE calibration is
due, Calib. Now is highlighted in yellow.
For ISE calibrations, the interval is predefined to 2 h.

About QC
The purpose of QC measurements is to monitor the
instrument performance. A QC measurement can be
ordered manually or automatically.

Automatic

Manual

Manual QC order

Automatic QC order

The system can automatically recommend tests for QC
measurements. To ensure correct results, you must
perform these recommended QC measurements before
starting operation. Additionally, the host can send an
order for QC measurements or you can order individual
tests for manual QC measurement.

QC measurements are typically ordered manually. There
are different reasons for performing manual QC
measurements:
•

If a QC result is outside the defined range, you can
perform the QC measurement again.

•

At the end of or during a shift, you can perform QC
measurements to verify the accuracy of the tests you
have been working on.

Depending on the configuration, the system can
automatically order QC measurements.

Roche Diagnostics
cobas® pro integrated solutions · Software version 03-03 · User Guide · Publication version 4.2

10 Non-routine operation

578

Failed

Changeover

Timeout

Update

If the QC indicator turns yellow, QC measurements of one
or more tests are recommended. Perform the QC
measurements for these tests before starting operation or
as soon as it fits into your operation workflow. Calibration
and QC must be completed successfully before operation.

Validation of QC

After measurement of QC material, the results are

a check mark in the Status column.
results of tests without check mark are
i QC

u Verifying QC results (462)

10 Non-routine operation

QC Chart

The QC chart (Routine > QC Chart) gives a graphical
overview on the deviation of the QC results from the target
value.
•

The horizontal axis shows the measurement sequence
from oldest result (left) to newest result (right).

•

The last 500 QC results for every test are displayed.

•

Only QC results having a numerical result are
displayed. Failed QC measurement without numerical
result are not displayed.

•

If you do not select a specific test or you select a test
using an asymmetric QC, the horizontal lines display
the Upper Limit, Target Mean, and Lower Limit.

•

If you select a specific test using only symmetric QC,
the horizontal lines display the 1SD, 2SD, 3SD, and
Target Mean.

•

The QC Chart also displays calculated QC results
with their QC points.
For calculated QC results, however, no reagent
information is displayed in the table below the chart as
for regular QC results. The only displayed information
is the name of the analytical unit.

•

If a data alarm is attached to the QC result, the QC
points are also displayed. The data alarm is displayed
in the table below the chart.

•

If you do not select a specific test, the QC results of
all tests and all analytical units are displayed.

•

If you select a test using the Select button, only the
QC results of the selected test are displayed and
vertical dotted lines are displayed. The first QC
measurement after one of the following events is
marked with a colored dotted line:
• Green: QC was performed after a reagent was
calibrated.

Roche Diagnostics
cobas® pro integrated solutions · Software version 03-03 · User Guide · Publication version 4.2

Non-routine operation

579

• Blue: QC was performed after a reagent in use
(Status: Current) was replaced or reloaded.
• Red: QC was performed after a reagent in use
(Status: Current) was replaced or reloaded and
calibrated.

not considered but only the selected point and older
data (from the selected point to the left).

delete respective QC measurement points in the QC chart.

Close

580

QC

Copy QC

One reagent can be assigned to multiple applications.
Each application needs a valid QC. Copy QC means that
the control unit applies QC results of the primary
application to up to 3 additional ACNs of the same
reagent.
To check whether a test uses copy QC, choose Routine >
Results for the test. From the options menu , choose
the Result Details button.
You can view the results of the copy QC in QC > QC
Chart. Copy QC is possible for current and standby
reagent packs.

Calculated QC

Linked kits and linked tests may provide a calculated QC
result. This QC result is based on individual tests from the
same lot and the same run. QC calculation is only
successful if QC results are available for all individual QC
tests.
Calculated QC results are displayed with their QC points
on Routine > QC Chart. For calculated QC results,
however, no reagent information is displayed in the table
below the chart as for regular QC results.

About QC types
The system supports various QC types for automatic and
manual QC measurements.
In the following cases, you must perform QC
measurements:
•

Each day before operation and at the end of
operation, to ensure accuracy during the entire
operation.

•

After calibration, to verify the calibration result.

•

When a new reagent is loaded to check the reagent.

•

After troubleshooting, to check the instrument
performance.

•

(ISE)
– When an electrode has been replaced.
– (ISE v1) When a wash rack maintenance has been
performed.

Roche Diagnostics
cobas® pro integrated solutions · Software version 03-03 · User Guide · Publication version 4.2

Non-routine operation

581

– (ISE neo) When an ISE System Wash has been
performed.
In addition, you can perform QC measurements anytime
during routine operation by selecting the QC types that
meet the requirements of your workflow.

Routine QC

With routine QC, you can order QC measurements for the
following:
•

all reagents in use (Status: Current)

•

all electrodes in use

Routine QC comprises all activated tests of all installed
QC materials and is usually performed before operation.
If you load QC material without a QC order onto the
system, the system can automatically order routine QC. To
use this function, you must select the Without Order,
Perform All Active Tests check box in the Calibration
and QC dialog box.
u Performing QC (459)
u Setting up automatic QC measurement requests (596)
With standby bottle QC, you can order QC measurements
for standby reagents. Standby reagents are reagent packs
that are already onboard but not in use.
If you order the QC measurements for standby reagents
together with the routine QC at the beginning of a work
shift, you do not need to perform a QC measurement
during operation when the status of the standby reagent
changes.
u Performing QC (459)
QC Now

To avoid QC measurements during operation, you can
perform QC measurements due in advance. To use this
function, select the Activate "QC Now" Cause check
box in the Calibration and QC dialog box.
On QC > Order, set the Remaining Time in hours to look
ahead. Then the system recommends a QC measurement
for any QC which times out in this time interval.
On QC > Order, the system recommends this QC type as
QC Now in the Cause column.
u Setting up the QC Now settings (599)

Standby Bottle QC

582

QC

QC after calibration

If you place a QC rack (white) directly after a calibrator
rack (black), the system automatically performs the QC
measurements for the calibrated tests (except for copied
calibrations). There is no need to configure settings in
advance or to order QC measurement.
QC after calibration can overlap the order of manual QC.
In this case, the system merges orders to become one.
STAT samples cannot interrupt the measurement of QC
after calibration. STAT samples are tested when the QC
measurements are complete.
QC after calibration is pipetted directly after the
calibrators. Therefore, the QC result might be calculated
even if the performed calibration failed. In this case, the
previous valid calibration is used for the calculation of the
QC result and the Cal.E data alarm is attached.

Calibration update

When the calibration of a reagent is updated, the related
reagent is patient masked. The system requests a QC
measurement for this reagent (indicated as Calibration
update in the Cause column).
transfer of a lot calibration to a newly loaded
i The
reagent pack is also considered as a calibration
update for this reagent pack.

Calibration and QC, then select the After Changing
Calibration Data check box.
To remove the automatic patient mask, you must perform
QC measurements of all QC materials for which the test is
activated. After the QC measurement, you must validate
the QC results.

About partner QC materials

10 Non-routine operation

Partner QC materials are non-Roche QC materials for
which the parameter file is available for download on
cobas® link.

Load-and-go processing

The system offers improved support for partner QC
material, so it can be used like Roche QC material.
You have to follow specific rules regarding the use of
container types and the loading on racks. As long as these
rules are applied, the system handles partner QC results in
the same way as QC results from Roche QC materials.

Roche Diagnostics
cobas® pro integrated solutions · Software version 03-03 · User Guide · Publication version 4.2

Non-routine operation

585

Container types and barcodes
Partner QC materials come in barcoded ø 13 x 75 mm
tubes.
direct use of the original ø 13 x 75 mm tubes is
i The
highly recommended.
Alternatively, for partner QC materials, you may use any of
the sample containers specified for other non-Roche QC
materials.
u Specifications of standard containers (102)
u False-bottom tubes (105)
QC racks

Always use separate QC racks for partner QC materials.
Do not load different QC material types (Roche QC, nonRoche QC, partner QC) on the same rack. In this case, the
system generates an alarm, unloads the rack, and QC
measurement does not take place.

Automatic QC container changeover

If the volume of a single tube is insufficient for all QC
measurements required, load a second tube of the same
QC lot into the next position on the same rack. The system
then automatically pipettes partner QC material from the
second tube when the first tube runs empty.

For container changeover, the system supports a
maximum of 2 containers with the same QC lot on a rack.

Download of parameter files

Download the parameter file for the partner QC material
from cobas® link.

the vendor of the partner QC material. If a value is not
available for a test, the system transfers 0.000100 as
target mean value or target SD value in the default unit.

Inactivating or activating tests for QC material
All tests onboard are automatically activated once the QC
material parameters are installed. If you do not want to
perform a QC measurement for a test, you can manually
inactivate this test.
If you have manually added QC material parameters, the
tests onboard are automatically inactivated. If you want to
perform a QC measurement for a test, you must activate
this test.

Setting up automatic QC measurement requests
Depending on the settings, the system automatically
requests QC measurements and masks a reagent for
patient samples.
Patient mask

If a reagent is patient masked, you can perform calibration
and QC measurement for this reagent but no patient
samples. To unmask the reagent, you must perform QC
measurements.
On Menu > System > Calibration and QC, you define
under which conditions the system automatically masks a
reagent and requests QC measurements:

10 Non-routine operation

After Loading/Reloading of Reagent check box:
The system generates a Changeover cause for a QC
measurement in the following cases:
•

When a reagent is registered or re-registered in the
system.

•

When QC material with a new material code is
registered or activated for the onboard reagent.

(ISE neo)
•

After replacement of ISE reagent or ISE electrode.

•

After ISE System Wash.

(ISE v1)
•

After replacement of ISE reagent or ISE electrode.

•

After wash rack maintenance.

Roche Diagnostics
cobas® pro integrated solutions · Software version 03-03 · User Guide · Publication version 4.2

Non-routine operation

597

After all related QC results are available, the following is
unmasked:
•

Reagent

•

(ISE) Electrodes

After Changing Calibration Data check box:
•

When the calibration of a reagent is updated, the
system generates a Calibration update cause for a
QC measurement.

•

The reagent is unmasked after all related QC results
are available.

After QC Interval Timeout check box:
•

After a QC timeout, the system generates a Timeout
cause for a QC measurement.

•

The reagent is unmasked after the sample supply unit
has registered all QC material containers related to
timeout QC.

After QC results with Data Alarms check box:
•

When the QC result fails, the system generates a
Failed cause for a QC measurement.

•

The reagent or electrode is unmasked after valid
results of all related QC measurements are available.

Different lots of a QC material with identical material
codes can be used to unmask patient masking.
Data alarms on QC results

A QC result with any data alarm is considered invalid.

•

Since a cobas® e flow test has no QC results, it
cannot be patient-masked. Only the embedded tests
are masked if there is an invalid QC result.

•

As a consequence, the sample is transferred to the
e 801 analytical unit but not fully processed due to
the masked embedded test. The cobas® e flow test
receives an eflowE data alarm in this case.

Setting up the QC timeout interval
QC measurements can be performed at predefined (testspecific) time intervals. When the time interval has
elapsed, the system recommends a QC measurement. To
use this function, you must enter the interval time on
Menu > Application > Analytical Parameters.
You can also activate the After QC Interval Timeout
check box on Menu > System > Calibration and QC.
When the time interval has elapsed, the related test gets
patient mask and the system orders a QC measurement.

Setting up the QC Now settings
The system can recommend a QC measurement when it is
due within the time you have defined. To use this function,
you must activate the QC Now function for the system
and define a remaining time interval.
If a QC measurement is due within the time defined on QC
> Order in the QC-now Timer: field, you can perform QC
measurement in advance. This QC measurement ensures
that you do not have to interrupt the operation for due QC
measurements.

for non-barcoded QC material, the rack will be unloaded
without QC measurement.

– You can assign the QC material to the QC racks.

Deleting QC material parameters
Before you download or add a QC material parameter, it is
recommended to delete any obsolete QC material
parameters.
You do not need to delete QC material parameters in the
following cases:
•

When you download a new QC lot.

•

When you download a new version number of the same
QC lot.

You can install up to 999 QC material parameters on the
system. When this limit is reached, you must first delete an
existing QC material parameter before installing a new
one.

discretion.

depending on specific conditions.

On Routine > Results > Result Details, the All Masks
dialog box displays the masks with highest priorities (up to
3 masks per analytical unit). If many masks are present at
the same time, additional low priority masks may be active
that are not displayed.
Masking functions are divided into 5 categories with
decreasing priority:
1. Analytical unit
2. Sample
3. Test
4. Reagents and consumables
5. Calibration and QC
Example: If test mask is active, lower priority masks of
categories 4 or 5 may be active but cannot be displayed
on the All Masks dialog box.

Test mask (manual)

To exclude a specific test from the current analysis
completely, you mask this test. For tests manually masked
in this way, the system does not process any sample
measurements, QC measurements, or calibrations.

The system masks a reagent pack automatically when it
has no valid calibration or the last calibration failed.
Administrators can disable automatic calibration masking
by a system-wide and a test-specific setting.
If both settings are on, masking is enabled:
•

The reagent or electrode is masked for routine or QC
samples processed after calibration is finished and
failed.

•

The Cal.E alarm is attached to results when routine or
QC samples are processed while the failing calibration
is still being performed.

QC mask

The system can mask a reagent pack for patient sample
measurements depending on the reagent’s QC status. The
system does not change to a standby reagent pack but
can request a QC measurement.

System > Calibration and QC.
In the following cases, the system can mask the reagent or
electrode and request a QC measurement depending on
the setting of the check boxes:
•

When a reagent is registered or re-registered in the
system.

When QC material with a new material code is

After calibrating a reagent.

Reagent mask

The system automatically masks a test when one of the
following conditions is met on a current reagent and no
standby reagent is on board:
•

A required reagent is empty.

•

A required reagent has expired (see next paragraph).

•

(CC) Air aspiration detected.

•

(e 801) Foam or film detected in reagent pack.

•

(e 801) The system could not link an assay reagent
pack to a required partner reagent pack or the partner
reagent is not on board.

Saving and backing up data
To protect data from accidental loss and to comply with
regulatory requirements for long-term retention, you must
store system data.
up your data (test results and system
i Back
parameters) at regular intervals.
the system has both a DVD and USB flash drive
i Ifavailable
at the same time, it uses the DVD as the
storage medium for certain saving functions.
To save data on a USB flash drive, ensure that no
DVD is inserted.

In this section
About saving and backing up data (613)
Saving sample records (615)
Displaying archived sample records (617)
Saving and deleting reports (618)
Working with storage media (621)

About saving and backing up data

Some data is stored by backup, some by saving:
•

A backup allows the system to recover deleted or
destroyed data.

•

Saving data provides access to data for a long time.

To minimize the risk of data loss, the system provides the
following storage routines:
•

Sample records: Uploading all test results to the host.
In addition, you can save copies to a storage medium
or a network storage (if enabled).

•

Database: The system backs up the database
(excluding sample records) automatically as part of
the self-operating maintenance.

•

Reports: Saving reports to a storage medium or a
network storage (if enabled).

About the automatic saving of sample records
Sample records are saved automatically by the selfoperating maintenance action sample records
management.
If you use the recommended settings, the system
automatically saves sample records in binary format and
clears the database in regular intervals. Your Roche
Service representative can set up the parameters
according to your needs.
u Related topics
• Moving internal sample data to storage media (668)

About output formats for saving sample records
The output format for saving sample records depends on
the target system you want to view the data on.

Binary format

The sample records are saved in binary format (*.mdf file
format). This format includes result details and reaction
monitor data and can only be viewed on the system. Other
PC systems cannot read this format. In Routine > Results
>
> Save, choose this output format with the Records
visible on System option.

Long-term formats

Comma-separated values (CSV) are a standardized format
that can be opened on any PC with standard spreadsheet
software. This format is suitable for long-term archiving
and is to be used exclusively for statistical evaluations and
throughput analyses. However, this format cannot be

cobas® pro integrated solutions · Software version 03-03 · User Guide · Publication version 4.2

opened on the system. In Routine > Results >
> Save,
choose this output format with the Results (CSV) or
Reaction Data (CSV) option.

Saving and deleting reports
To reduce the data volume on the instrument, you can
save and delete reports.
When the stored reports in Report > Display occupy
more than 500 MB, the system issues an alarm. Regardless
of this alarm, the system still saves new reports.
By default, reports remain available even after the system
is switched off.

Formatting a DVD‑RAM
When you format a DVD-RAM, the system deletes all
stored data.
Before you format the DVD‑RAM, ensure that there is no
important data on a used DVD‑RAM.

NOTICE!
Data loss due to poor quality DVD-RAMs
Scratched or dirty DVD-RAMs can lead to data loss.
r If a DVD-RAM is scratched or dirty, discard it and use a
new one.

About connecting and disconnecting USB flash drives
Only connect or disconnect USB flash drives while the
system is in Standby mode. To disconnect USB flash
drives, always use the Eject USB Flash Drive button.
Connecting or disconnecting USB flash drives during
operation might slow down the control unit and interfere
with the processing of results.

Disconnecting USB flash drives without choosing the
Eject USB Flash Drive button first, might cause data
loss.
Never shut the system down with a connected USB flash
drive.
u Related topics
• Formatting a USB flash drive (623)

Shutting down or switching on the system
The system is intended for continuous operation (24/7).
Shutting down

If you must shut down the system, choose the relevant
procedure based on the duration for which you plan to
shut it down:

To shut down

Relevant procedure

For < 64 hours

u Shutting down the system (627)

For > 64 hours

u Shutting down for 64 hours to 17 days (630)

For certain maintenance actions

u Shutting down the system for maintenance (670)

y Overview of shutdown procedures

When the system has shut down, the electrical power is
not switched off completely: The power supply is
disconnected from all outer components, so that you can
move, for example, pipetter arms for manual cleaning.
However, some internal components such as the reagent
cooling are still supplied with power even when the system
has shut down.
Choose the switch-on procedure based on the duration for
which the system has been shut down or switched off
completely:

To switch on

Relevant procedure

After < 24 hours of shutdown

u Switching on after less than 24 hours of shutdown (635)

After > 24 hours of shutdown

u Switching on after 24 to 64 hours of shutdown (637)

After > 64 hours of shutdown

u Switching on after 64 hours to 17 days of shutdown (639)

After certain maintenance actions

u Switching on the system after maintenance (671)

y Overview of switch-on procedures

Switching off the system completely

If you must switch off the system completely for some
reason, do the following:
1. Unload all reagent packs and store them refrigerated.
2. Follow the procedure for shutting down the system
corresponding to the planned shutdown duration.
3. To switch off the system completely after the
shutdown, operate the circuit breaker.

Working with a laboratory automation system

Sample processing

If there is a connection to an LAS, the function of the STAT
port changes. The STAT port is used to transport routine
samples from the LAS to the instrument.
If you have STAT samples, place the STAT samples on a
red STAT rack. Place the STAT rack on the loading lane of
the sample supply unit or to the STAT port of the LAS.

Sample unloading with A-gate

If there is a connection to a unidirectional LAS (A-gate), all
samples are unloaded to the unloading lanes of the
sample supply unit.

Sample unloading with B-gate

If there is a connection to a bidirectional LAS (B-gate),
samples are transferred back to the LAS.
If the LAS stops working, rack will be unloaded to the
unloading lanes of the sample supply unit.
For faster access to problematic samples, your Roche
Service representative can set up automatic sample
unloading to the sample supply unit for the following
samples:
•

Samples with barcode read error

•

Samples with sample volume error or sample clot

•

Samples with error detected by the cup height sensor
(e.g., sample container of an unexpected type, or
incorrectly placed on the rack)

Contact your Roche Service representative to configure
the system for automatic sample unloading.

Guidance for blood donation screening –

To ensure and confirm the validity of test results, some
provisions should be considered when using the e 801
analytical unit for donation screening applications. This
section has been prepared to highlight these
considerations and to support regulatory requirements.
For more information on using the e 801 analytical unit for
donation screening applications, refer to the following
documents:
•

Guide to the preparation, use and quality assurance of
BLOOD COMPONENTS, European Committee (Partial
Agreement) on Blood Transfusion (CD-P-TS), EDQM,
18th ed. 2015; 204–206.

•

Directive 2005/62/EC Annex 6.2. and 6.5.

•

Successful Barcode Reading. Roche Diagnostics
International Ltd., 2016.

•

The collection, testing and use of BLOOD AND BLOOD
COMPONENTS in Europe, European Committee
(Partial Agreement) on Blood Transfusion (CD-P-TS),
EDQM, 2013 Report;6.

•

Consider respective local legislation outside EU+EFTA
countries.

In this section

10 Non-routine operation

Quick reference: Performing QC before and after a sample
run – e 801 (650)
Quick reference: Activating barcode mode for all samples
run within the blood bank – e 801 (652)

Quick reference: Performing QC before and after a
sample run – e 801
For each assay, Roche provides QC materials to be
measured before and after testing the donor sample. In
addition, every laboratory can choose to run non-Roche
QC material in order to evaluate assays and the system
reliability. The QC materials are used to verify the
calibration curve and ensure the accuracy of the
calculated sample results based on this calibration curve.
The target values of QC materials have to be recovered
within a defined range and these results are used to
monitor the accuracy and precision of tests.

Roche Diagnostics
cobas® pro integrated solutions · Software version 03-03 · User Guide · Publication version 4.2

Non-routine operation

651

Sample results must be released based on QC results that
are run before and after sample measurement. The
purpose of this testing is to monitor the instrument and
assay function for systematic errors. This procedure is
called QC bracketing, and it ensures generating reliable
donation results.
Timing and testing intervals depend on the laboratories’
workflow and have to be defined by the customer
accordingly. QC materials include positive and negative
QC material. If antigens and antibodies are tested in
parallel, positive QC material should be tested covering
both applications.
Testing of negative QC material may be replaced by other
methodologies (e.g., moving median approach) and is left
to the discretion of the customer.

measurement.

4.

Only if both QC measurements are within
their limits, release the sample results.

Overview of maintenance
