Maintenance definitions
User maintenance actions can be divided into selfoperating maintenance, software-controlled maintenance,
and manual maintenance.

Software-controlled maintenance

Maintenance actions that are scheduled and are
performed automatically by the system without any
operator interaction.

Maintenance actions that are performed by the system.
They can be divided into 2 categories.
•

Fully automatic maintenance, i.e. without operator
interaction.
Fully automatic maintenance actions can be started
either by the operator or by a maintenance pipe.

•

Interactive maintenance (semi-automatic or guided
maintenance actions), i.e. with operator interaction.
While an interactive maintenance action is running,
you can perform other tasks. When your action is
required, the Maintenance button turns blue.

Background maintenance

Maintenance action that is performed on a masked
analytical unit while other analytical units are operating.

Parallel maintenance

Different maintenance actions are performed
simultaneously on different analytical units of a system in
parallel.

Integrated maintenance

Software-controlled maintenance action that is part of
another maintenance action and started automatically by
the system during the sequential performance of the other
maintenance action.

Manual maintenance

Maintenance actions that you perform manually (for
example, cleaning the instrument surface).

time intervals, measuring count, or for a specific system
mode.
When your system was initially configured, your Roche

actions according to your requirements.

maintenance action, contact your Roche Service
representative.

About sample records management
The system automatically saves sample records that are
no longer required to a backup medium. The sample
records are then deleted from the system database to
free up storage space. The system database has only a
limited capacity for measurement data to allow fast data
access.
You can configure the following settings:
•

Execution time:
– Select a time at which the device is switched on
but a low workload is expected.
Note:
– If the system is not in a suitable operating mode at
the set execution time, backup and deletion of
sample records is postponed until the system
reaches Standby or Rack Reception mode. To
inform the user, the system alarm "Sample Records
Management rescheduled" is generated

11 Overview of maintenance

– If the system is switched off at the set execution
time, backup, and deletion of sample records is
skipped on this day.
•

Desired sample statuses for saving and deleting
targets:
– Sent to Host
– Complete
– Incomplete

•

Data retention period:
– Minimum time before sample records are deleted

•

Target backup medium:
– USB flash drive
– Internal hard disk
– Network storage (if enabled)

About back up database
If the system must be restored for any reason, a database
backup can be used (service logon required). If automatic
backups by self-operating maintenance are enabled, a
database backup is saved regularly to the service USB
flash drive.
The system backs up the database to the service USB
flash drive the next time the system enters Rack
Reception mode after 24 hours have elapsed.

For example, if you load new samples while the system is in
Rack Reception mode, back up database is interrupted
(if active). In this case, the system restarts database
backup from the beginning the next time the system enters
Rack Reception mode.
The database backup does not contain sample records.

i •

When the Enable Lab Automation
Connection option is enabled, automatic
backups are never performed as the system
does not reach Rack Reception mode.

•

Backup should regularly be started manually
(Maintenance > Checks > 26 Back up
Database).

About reagent prime - ISE v1
This maintenance action primes the flow paths of the ISE
reagents.
When the ISE analytical unit has been in Standby mode
for 5 h, the system automatically performs this
maintenance action before entering Operation mode
again.

If disabled

If the ISE reagent prime has been disabled in the SOM
settings, you must perform the maintenance action 8
Prime System Reagents Flow Path manually every day
using the default options.

About ISE System Wash - ISE neo
The system washes and conditions the ISE reagent flow
paths at the defined wash interval automatically. Only the
Roche Service representative can adjust the interval within
a 24 to 48 hour range.
If you have not run an ISE System Wash within the
defined interval, the system masks the analytical unit.

11 Overview of maintenance

ISE System Wash can be performed with different wash
intensities. Only Roche Service representatives can view
and change the wash intensity.

To check the interval settings, choose Menu > System >
ISE System Wash.

About system wash
CC

While operating, the system washes all reaction cells.
Afterwards, the system performs a cell blank
measurement.

11 Overview of maintenance

(c 503) The system processes 44 or 45 of the 221
reaction cells per day.
(c 703) The system processes 81 or 82 of the 406
reaction cells per day.
After the system has been switched on for 5 days, all cells
have been processed and the cycle repeats.
Unwashed reaction cells are never used for measurement.
Before using reaction cells for measurement, the system
automatically checks for and, if necessary, schedules
system wash. If cleaning solution is low or missing, the
system generates an alarm. If Basic Wash and NaOHD are
missing, the system will not start.
The system uses 12 wavelengths to perform the cell blank
measurement. If the absorbance result for a reaction cell
differs more than 0.1 from reaction cell number 1, this
reaction cell is determined as abnormal and the system
generates an alarm.

About masking an analytical unit
To perform maintenance on one analytical unit while the
rest of the system is operating, you can mask this
analytical unit. A masked analytical unit remains in
Standby mode and is unavailable for operation.

Roche Diagnostics
cobas® pro integrated solutions · Software version 03-03 · User Guide · Publication version 4.2

11 Overview of maintenance

5 Enter your user ID and password and choose the Log

User

672

About system modes for maintenance

Performing maintenance on one analytical unit while the
rest of the system is operating is called background
maintenance.
To mask an analytical unit, the system can be in Standby
mode. But you can also mask an analytical unit during most
operational and maintenance modes. An analytical unit
can be masked without the sample buffer. This way, the
sample buffer can operate while the analytical unit is
masked.
However, upon masking one analytical unit for background
maintenance, the samples for that unit can no longer be
processed. You must load these samples again.
If the system consists of several identical analytical units
and you mask one of them, the system processes the
samples on the other analytical units. However, if the
reagents for a test are unavailable on the other analytical
units, the test is masked and you must load these samples
again.

Limitations of masking - ISE v1

The c 503 analytical unit and the associated ISE analytical
unit to the left share the same sample buffer. The c 503
analytical unit supplies water, vacuum, and Basic Wash
solution to the associated ISE analytical unit.

11 Overview of maintenance

Therefore, maintenance is limited by these shared
resources. For this reason, some maintenance actions
cannot be performed on the c 503 analytical unit while the
associated ISE analytical unit is operating or performing a
maintenance action.
The following maintenance actions are subject to this
limitation:
•

45 Photometer Unit Maintenance

•

5 Exchange Incubation Bath Water

•

10 Clean Incubation Bath Manually

•

12 Replace Reaction Cells

•

13 Replace Photometer Lamp

•

9 Prime Wash Solutions Flow Paths

•

Any maintenance with rack

Furthermore, the ISE analytical unit cannot switch to
Operation mode while the c 503 analytical unit remains
masked, due to the shared resources. Both analytical units
have to switch to Operation mode at the same time.
To perform these maintenance actions, you must mask the
ISE analytical unit together with the c 503 analytical unit.

Roche Diagnostics
cobas® pro integrated solutions · Software version 03-03 · User Guide · Publication version 4.2

Overview of maintenance

Maintenance pipes cannot be performed as background
maintenance. You must perform all maintenance actions
individually.

About parallel maintenance
You can use parallel maintenance to perform different
maintenance actions simultaneously on different
analytical units.
For parallel maintenance, the respective analytical units
must be in Standby mode. Then, you can perform
maintenance actions on more than one analytical unit.
Maintenance pipe functions cannot be performed as
parallel maintenance. You must perform all maintenance
actions individually.
You can cancel maintenance actions performed on a
specific analytical unit.

• List of system modes (256)

What are maintenance pipes and maintenance pipe
functions?
During continuous operation, you do not necessarily need
to use maintenance pipes. But you can use them to
optimize your laboratory workflow. If you work in shifts,
maintenance pipes and maintenance pipe functions are
useful.

You can group maintenance actions into maintenance
pipes. The system can then perform all maintenance
actions in the maintenance pipe automatically without
operator intervention.
Maintenance pipes can be performed in 2 different ways:
•

Manually by operators

•

Automatically using maintenance pipe functions

14 Back up System Configuration

The parameters of the system settings are backed up to or restored from a storage medium

different parts manually, for example, the pipetters, for cleaning purposes, without having
to shut down the system.

QC materials via the 2D barcode reader on cobas® pro SSU.

List of user maintenance and checks

Maintenance action

Description

4 Cell Blank Measurement

Cell blank values of all reaction cells are measured. If the absorbance result for a reaction
cell differs more than 0.1 from reaction cell no. 1, this cell is determined as abnormal cell
and the system generates an alarm.
On Report > Display > Cell Blank Measurement Report, the system automatically
displays the measured absorbance values of cell number 1 at 12 wavelengths and the
reaction cell numbers determined to be abnormal.

5 Exchange Incubation Bath Water

The incubation bath water is exchanged and EcoTergent is added. If EcoTergent is low or
missing, the maintenance action is not performed and an alarm is issued.
To inform you that this maintenance is due again, the system issues the following alarms:
•

6 days after the last execution: a warning, once

•

7 days after the last execution until the maintenance action is performed again: daily
warnings

6 Air Purge

An air purge preserves the pipetting precision. To remove air bubbles, the pipetting flow
path is filled with degassed water. Water and air are discharged at the rinse stations.

9 Prime Wash Solutions Flow Paths

The wash solutions flow paths are primed using the selected detergent. You can select
Basic Wash, Acid Wash, or both as wash solution.

10 Clean Incubation Bath Manually

The photometer lamp is switched off and the incubation bath water is drained. You must
complete and confirm the incubation bath cleaning. Then, the system refills the incubation
bath and adds EcoTergent.
If EcoTergent is low or missing, the maintenance action is not performed and an alarm is
issued.
The maintenance action 10 Clean Incubation Bath Manually is part of 45 Photometer
Unit Maintenance which is recommended for the manual cleaning of the incubation bath.

11 Overview of maintenance

12 Replace Reaction Cells

The motor of the reaction disk of the specified analytical unit is switched off and the
reaction disk can be moved freely. Use this maintenance action to replace all reaction cell
segments without having to shut down the system.
After reaction cells replacement, the system performs the maintenance actions 17
System Wash and 4 Cell Blank Measurement automatically.
To inform you that this maintenance is due again, the system issues the following alarms:
•

29 days after the last execution: a warning, once

•

30 days after the last execution until the maintenance action is performed again: daily
warnings

The maintenance action 12 Replace Reaction Cells is an optional part of 45
Photometer Unit Maintenance which is recommended to use for the replacement of
reaction cells.

Maintenance action

Description

13 Replace Photometer Lamp

The photometer lamp is switched off. Use this maintenance action to replace the
photometer lamp without having to shut down the system.

system automatically performs the maintenance action 4 Cell Blank Measurement.

697

The sample probe S2 is washed in the wash station using Basic Wash solution. The sample

42 Replace and Adjust or Unclog
Probes

With the Sample Probe 1 (eliminate clogging only) option, use this maintenance action
to eliminate clogging in the S1 sample probe or to clean this probe manually.
When the sample probe is back in place, perform the maintenance action 4 Probe Check
manually.
If you continue to use the same probe, probe adjustment is not required.
With the Sample Probe 2 option, use this maintenance action to replace the S2 sample
probe, or to eliminate clogging in this probe, or to clean this probe manually.
The maintenance action integrates the 4 Probe Check and probe adjustment after
replacing, or unclogging, or manual cleaning of the S2 sample probe.
Note: If remote screen sharing is enabled, the system notifies you before automatically
disabling the remote connection for the duration of this maintenance action.

43 Start Water Bath Circulation

An interruption of the system initialization may prevent the start of the incubation bath
circulation. If the initialization of the system has been interrupted for any reason, perform
this maintenance action separately.

deionized water and then filled with air. Specify the number of rinse cycles.

26 Wash Sippers Flow Paths

With the ECL option, the ECL sipper flow paths in the detection unit are washed with
SysClean solution.
With the Pre-Wash option, the flow path of the pre-wash sipper nozzle is washed with
SysClean solution. This maintenance action must be performed after
10 000 measurements for each ECL sipper flow path and after 20 000 measurements for
the pre-wash flow path. To enable you to plan this maintenance, the system issues a yellow
alarm as a pre-warning, 700 measurements before the specified intervals (at 9300 and
19 300 measurements, respectively).
The control unit will reset the test counter for this maintenance action after you have
performed it. Specify the number of wash cycles.

11 Overview of maintenance

27 Update Inventory

The number of full and empty tip and cup trays is updated. The number of tips and cups is
verified for the current tray. If the number is lower than expected by the software, the tips
or cups are discarded from the current tray. Then, a full tip and cup tray is lifted to the top.
The fill levels of the solid waste boxes and of the system reagents PreClean II M,
ProCell II M, and CleanCell M are updated.
In addition, you can select the Register cobas e packs check box to perform a reagent
RFID check.

29 Rinse Pre-wash Sipper Flow Path

The pre-wash sipper nozzle and flow paths are rinsed with deionized water. The pre-wash
sipper flow paths are purged of air. Specify the number of cycles.

31 Finalization

The finalization routine is carried out on the sample pipetter, reagent pipetter, ECL sipper
nozzles, PreClean supply nozzle, pre-wash sipper nozzle, detection unit, and system
reagents. The analytical unit replaces system reagents in the ProCell/CleanCell cups and
fills the measuring cells with deionized water.

32 Empty ProCell and CleanCell Cups The ProCell/CleanCell cups are drained.
35 Remove AssayCups from
Incubator

The system removes and discards all cups that have already been placed to positions on
the analytical unit (from the incubator disk, the vortex mixers, separation stations, and
AssayCup holders). If cups remain on the analytical unit, for example, after an emergency
stop, you can use this maintenance action.

25 Sync with cobas link

Initiates parameter synchronization between cobas® link and the control unit. New or
updated parameters for applications, calibrators, QC materials, and special washes are
then available under Pre-Routine > Download Required Items.
Parameters are automatically synchronized once per day and during the power-up of the
system. This maintenance check allows initiating an additional synchronization.

calibration and QC result data, but without sample records on the service USB flash drive.

34 Water Quality Check

This function detects a potential influence on ISE results due to poor water quality.
Different dilution steps of ISE Internal Standard (diluted with system water) are measured
with the Na, K, Cl electrodes and a slope in mV/dec is generated. The values can give an
indication whether or not ions are in the water.
The slope in mV/dec has to be within the following ranges:
Na: 40 < slope ≤ 68
K: 40 < slope ≤ 68
Cl: -35 > slope ≥ -68
A report is generated automatically and a Slope.E data alarm indicates that the check was
out of range.
Note: The slope for water quality check may be affected by the condition of the
measurement system including electrodes.

List of cleaning solutions

List of cleaning solutions
When cleaning or decontaminating the system, use the
recommended substances listed below.
Repeated use of alcohol or bleach on the instrument
surface may damage the surface finish. For this reason,
use alcohol and bleach only to clean up spills but not for
regular cleaning.
For regular cleaning, such as removing dust from the
instrument surface, use deionized water only.
•

Alcohol (e.g., isopropyl alcohol or ethanol)
Recommended concentration: 70%
Note: Alcohol solutions between 60% and 80% are
known to be rapidly antimicrobial against bacteria,
fungi, and viruses. Alcohol solutions with a
concentration below 50% or above 90% are not
suitable.

•

2% EcoTergent solution
EcoTergent is supplied in concentrated form. You
must dilute it with deionized water at a ratio of 1:50 to
a 2% solution.

11 Overview of maintenance

Diluted EcoTergent solutions are stable for 3 weeks.
•

ISE Cleaning Solution/Elecsys SysClean solution

•

Deproteinizer

•

0.5% sodium hypochlorite solution (NaClO)

•

2% sodium hypochlorite solution (NaClO)

•

Laboratory disinfectant

•

Deionized water

•

Tap water

keeps the risk of contamination low. Follow the

The listed maintenance intervals are independent of the
operating time, unless otherwise noted.

Exchanging the incubation water – c 503
EcoTergent is added to the incubation water to prevent
bacterial growth. The incubation water must be exchanged
weekly because the antibacterial effect decreases over
time.
(ISE v1) The weekly wash rack maintenance automatically
triggers an incubation water exchange (on the connected
c 503) when more than 24 hours have elapsed since the

Performing maintenance of the photometric system –
c 503
To perform maintenance of the photometric system,
perform the following procedures monthly in the given
order displayed on the left.

Replacing the photometer lamp is required after 750 h of
switch-on time or every 6 months.

Performing maintenance of the photometric system

•

After 725 h, the system generates a yellow system
alarm.

•

After 750 h, the yellow alarm becomes persistent,
that is, even if you delete the alarm, the alarm will
come up again until you have replaced the lamp
successfully.

1

Prepare maintenance of the photometric system

2

Remove the wash unit and reaction cell covers

3

Remove the reaction disk

When you replace the photometer lamp, however, do so as
part of this monthly maintenance and not separately.

4

Replace the reaction cell segments

5

Clean the incubation bath

To check the current switch-on time of the photometer
lamp and the previous usage time of the reaction cells,
choose the Overview button.

6

Replace the photometer lamp
(required after 750 h of power-on time)

Infection and injury due to contact with system
mechanisms

7

Reinstall the reaction disk

Contact with the sampling mechanism or other
mechanisms may lead to biohazardous contamination,
resulting in personal injury and/or infection.

8

Clean the reaction cell covers and ultrasonic mixer
covers

r Before starting any maintenance, ensure that all
covers are closed and locked.

9

Reinsert the reaction cell covers and wash unit

corresponding analytical unit into an appropriate
mode. The appropriate modes are described in the

parts specified.

Emptying and cleaning the liquid waste containers
When you empty the liquid waste containers, also clean
them at the same time.
waste containers are optional and will be
i Liquid
installed by your Roche Service representative

only in cases where the highly concentrated liquid
waste of the analytical unit cannot be drained into
the laboratory's drainage system.

WARNING!
Infectious waste
Contact with waste (liquid and/or solid) may result in
infection. All materials and mechanical components
associated with the waste systems are potentially
biohazardous.
r Wear appropriate personal protective equipment.
r Take extra care when working with lab gloves. They can
easily be pierced or cut.
r If any biohazardous material is spilled, wipe it up
immediately and apply a disinfectant.
r If waste comes into contact with your skin, wash the
affected area immediately with soap and water and
apply a disinfectant. Consult a physician.

You can neutralize unpleasant odors emitted from the
liquid waste of the e 801 analytical unit using citric acid,
for example, 1 g citric acid monohydrate per 1 liter of
concentrated waste.

When a liquid waste container is full, perform this
maintenance action.

12 Maintenance actions

If a liquid waste container is full, the system issues the
system alarm "exchange waste tank". If both liquid waste
containers are full, the system enters S. Stop mode or
Stop mode depending on which analytical unit is affected.
If there is no liquid waste container present at all, the
system enters E.Stop mode.

About replacing the photometer lamp – c 503
Replacing the photometer lamp is required after 750 h of
power-on time or every 6 months.

12 Maintenance actions

After 725 h, the system generates a yellow system alarm.
After 750 h, the yellow alarm becomes persistent, that is,
even if you delete the alarm, the alarm will come up again
until you have replaced the lamp successfully.
If you replace the photometer lamp, you do so as part of
the maintenance of the photometric system, not as an
individual maintenance action. You must perform the
maintenance of the photometric system monthly.
u Related topics
• Performing maintenance of the photometric system –
c 503 (795)

Exchanging the incubation water – c 703
EcoTergent is added to the incubation water to prevent
bacterial growth. The incubation water must be exchanged
monthly because the antibacterial effect decreases over
time.
The incubation water is also exchanged during the monthly
maintenance of the photometric system.
To inform you that this maintenance is due, the system
issues the following alarms:

c
n
d
j

•

29 days after the last execution: a warning, once

•

30 days after the last execution until the maintenance
action is performed: daily warnings

If you have not performed the monthly maintenance of the
photometric system, perform this maintenance action
separately.
System time: approximately 18 min (not including the time
to reach 37 °C)

Alarm-specific remedies

Alarms

If any abnormality occurs while the system is switched on,
the system notifies the operator of the potential problem
by issuing an alarm.

To indicate a system alarm, the Alarms button is colored
yellow or red.
Read the description of the issued alarm and follow the
recommended remedy.
In addition to system alarms, result-related problems are
indicated by data alarms on Routine > Results.
u About data alarms and system alarms (967)

interactive help topics:

2. Choose the

order.

issue and follow the guided steps until it is solved.

Service representative.

Introduction to troubleshooting

967

About data alarms and system alarms
If the system detects an irregularity, it notifies the
operator of the potential problem by issuing an alarm.

Alarm types and levels

Type

Alarms are classified into different types and severities:
•

Data alarms indicate irregular measuring conditions or
results.

•

System alarms indicate irregular system conditions.

Severity

Meaning

Data alarm

Data alarms are related to the results of calibrations, QC, or samples. The system
does not stop operation.

Data alarms:

System alarms:
Caution

This alarm is triggered by data alarms or problems with the system. If this alarm
occurs during operation, the system does not stop operation. As a user, you must
judge whether to continue or interrupt the sample processing.
In addition, this alarm level is used to inform users about maintenance intervals (due
soon or exceeded) or finished events.

S.Stop
(Sampling stop)

This alarm is related to problems with the system. The affected analytical unit stops
sampling for new measurements. For pipetted samples, the measurements
continue.

Stop

This alarm is related to problems with the system. The corresponding analytical unit
or the entire system stops operation. For the sample under measurement, no result
data are collected and the measurement must be repeated.

E.Stop
(Emergency stop)

This alarm is triggered by hardware failures or if any of the safety devices
requested an emergency stop. The system requires either a complete shutdown, or
at least a reset to resume normal operation.

y Alarm types and levels

Data alarms

Data alarms are attached to the corresponding test result,
indicated on Routine > Results and on reports as well as
sent to the host.
Some data alarms can trigger an automatic rerun test.
u List of data alarms that generate an automatic rerun
test (1052)

System alarms

Alarms

System alarms are indicated by the Alarms button.

The color of the Alarms button indicates the severity:

Roche Diagnostics
cobas® pro integrated solutions · Software version 03-03 · User Guide · Publication version 4.2

13 Introduction to troubleshooting

This alarm is also generated when the system starts monitoring or finishes some
actions.

968

About data alarms and system alarms

Yellow: Operation can be continued (caution).
Red: Operation cannot be continued (S.Stop, Stop, or
E.Stop).

Safety shutdown for frozen user interface

Safety shutdown for frozen user interface
If the user interface freezes and the system becomes
inoperable for an extended time period, the safety
shutdown allows for a safe recovery of the system.
Forcing a system restart by pressing and holding the
power button risks damaging the PC of the control unit.
Safety shutdown forces the application to shut down in a
safe manner and shortens the recovery time after a
freeze.

r To activate the safety shutdown

yyyy/mm/dd

13 Introduction to troubleshooting

06:53

Confirmation
To force a shutdown of the control unit PC, choose the Confirm button. After the control unit has shut down, do the following:
a. Press and hold the OPERATION POWER button on the Sample Supply Unit for 10 seconds to turn off the instrument.
b. After turning off the instrument, wait 30 seconds.
c. To restart the system, choose the OPERATION POWER button to restart the system.

Cancel

975

Restarting an analytical unit after stop
alarm
If an AU-specific stop alarm occurs, the analytical unit
enters Standby mode (not masked) while the rest of the
system is operating. By masking and unmasking, you can
put this analytical unit back to operation without putting
the complete system to Standby mode.
The system generates AU-specific stop alarms, for
example, when a system reagent is empty or both waste
containers are full. Then this analytical unit is isolated
from the system. In this case, the analytical unit cannot be
restarted with the Start button.

j

m Stop system alarm is displayed for an analytical unit.
m The affected analytical unit is in Standby mode and
not masked while the system is operating.

r To restart an analytical unit
1 To mask the affected analytical unit, choose Start >
Masking > Mask Unit.

AU

SB

AU

SB

Masked

Not masked

Masked

Service
masked

2 Choose the button of the analytical unit until the
Masked option is displayed.
I The Service masked option is for Roche Service
representatives only.
3 Choose the Save button.
4 Wait until the affected analytical unit is masked
(indicated by a gray cross ).
5 Choose the Alarms button.
6 To resolve the reason for the stop alarm, perform the
remedy described in the Alarms dialog box.
7 To unmask the affected analytical unit:
• Choose Start > Masking > Mask Unit.
• Choose the button of the analytical unit repeatedly
until the Not masked option is displayed.
• Choose the Save button.
f

(green dotted cross): The analytical unit is being
unmasked.

f

analytical unit takes over the status of the system.

Priorities for data alarms

be associated with a test result. The data alarm with the
highest priority is displayed on Routine > Results and on
reports.
In the Data Alarms dialog box available in the Test
Result Details screen, you can see all data alarms of a
test result sorted by their priority.
All data alarms are transferred to the host in the order of
the alarm priority.

WB.T (1032)

994

Data alarms for tests

Remedy

•

The sample concentration is too high or the sample is
lipemic.

•

The reagent has not been stored or handled properly.

•

Obstructions are in the optical path of the
photometer.

(CC)
1. If only one sample is affected: Check whether the
sample is grossly lipemic or has a high value. Follow
your laboratory protocol for this situation.
2. If only one test is affected, perform the respective QC
to verify reagent conditions. Check reagent storage
and handling for that test.
3. If all samples are affected, do the following:
– Choose Report > Settings > Photometer
Check Report (SOM).
– Check the report. If the current results exceed
1.4 Abs. at any wavelength or differ significantly
from the previous results, do the following:
– Perform Maintenance > 45 Photometer Unit
Maintenance. Make sure that the reaction cells,
the incubation bath, and the photometer windows
are free of contamination and air bubbles.
– (c 503) Perform Maintenance > Checks > 30
Photometer Check. If the results are not
improved compared to the previous report,
replace the photometer lamp.
– (c 703) Perform Maintenance > Checks > 30
Photometer Check. If the results are not
improved compared to the previous report, please
contact your Roche Service representative.
4. If samples are affected intermittently:
Check the reaction cells for damage; if any reaction
cell is scratched, replace all reaction cells.

14 Data alarms

5. Resume operation. If the alarm recurs, contact your
Roche Service representative.
u Performing maintenance of the photometric system –
c 503 (795)
u Performing maintenance of the photometric system –
c 703 (808)

1000

Data alarms for tests

Description

If the cell blank value of a reaction cell differs from the
reference (stored value from the cell blank maintenance)
by more than 0.1 Abs., the system excludes this reaction
cell from measurements.
For diluted tests, however, the system uses 2 reaction
cells with a fixed distance:
•

First reaction cell: Contains sample and diluent.

•

Second reaction cell: Used for discharging diluted
sample from the first reaction cell, adding reagent,
and measurement.

Due to the fixed distance between predilution and the
measuring cell, the system cannot use another measuring
cell for the measurement of the prediluted sample.
Therefore, the measurement is canceled.
The >Cuvet alarm indicates a failed cell blank
measurement for the second reaction cell.

Cause

Remedy

(CC)
•

Reaction cells are contaminated or damaged.

•

Particles in the incubation water bath.

(CC)
1. Check the tubings of the wash unit. Ensure that no
tubing is bent.
2. Ensure that there is no excessive foaming or particles
in the incubation bath.
– Remove a reaction cell segment.
– Do not touch the optical surfaces of the reaction
cells.

14 Data alarms

– Ensure that no water drops adhering to the outside
of the reaction cells drip onto components.
3. If you notice excessive foaming or particles, perform
Maintenance > 10 Clean Incubation Bath
Manually.
• The system drains the water from the incubation
bath.
• To disassemble the wash unit and reaction cells,
refer to the description of the monthly photometer
unit maintenance.
• In addition, clean the outside of the reaction cells
with a lint-free cloth moistened with deionized
water.

Roche Diagnostics
cobas® pro integrated solutions · Software version 03-03 · User Guide · Publication version 4.2

Data alarms

1001

4. Perform Maintenance > 4 Cell Blank
Measurement.
5. Resume operation. If the alarm recurs, perform
Maintenance > 12 Replace Reaction Cells.
You must replace all reaction cell segments because
the day counter is reset to 0 for all reaction cells.
Otherwise, some segments would be used too long
(more than 30 days).
After the replacement, the system performs the
maintenance actions 17 System Wash and 4 Cell
Blank Measurement automatically.
6. Resume operation. If the alarm recurs, contact your
Roche Service representative.
u Performing maintenance of the photometric system –
c 503 (795)
u Performing maintenance of the photometric system –

Calibration data alarms

List of calibration data alarms (1045)

Cal.E
Alarm

Description

CALIB error (for calibrations)

The calibrator S3 concentration value deviates from the
specified limits.
The S3 concentration is checked by a relative and an
absolute check. The limits for both checks are specified on
Menu > Application > ISE > Application in the
Calibration Error area.

Cause

Remedy

•

Relative check: The deviation in mmol/L between the
current and the previous concentration must be
smaller than the Deviation: limit.

•

Absolute check: The S3 concentration must be within
the permissible range.

•

If one of the checks fails, the Cal.E alarm is issued.

(ISE)
•

The S3 calibrator solution has become concentrated
or degenerated.

•

The S3 calibrator solution or reagent is not placed in
proper position.

•

The ISE reagents have deteriorated.

•

There is a problem with the electrode.

(ISE)
1. Prepare fresh calibrators and recalibrate the ISE unit.

14 Data alarms

2. Correct any other system alarm and/or data alarms.
3. Check calibrators and reagents. If calibrators and
reagents are acceptable, resume operation.
Otherwise, correct abnormalities and recalibrate.
4. If the alarm recurs, replace the electrode.

Dup.E
Alarm

Description

Duplicate error

(CC)
The difference between the first and second measurement
(absorbance) of a calibrator is outside the specified range.
The following steps describe how a decision is made to
mark a calibration for violating the duplicate limit.
1. The absorbance for a calibrator (N) is measured twice.
2. The % of error and absorbance error are calculated.
3. Is the absorbance error smaller than the Duplicate
Limit: (Abs.) field on Menu > Application > cAU >
Calibration?
– If no, go to step 5.
4. Continue with result calculations. No Dup.E alarm is
issued.
5. Is the % error < the Duplicate Limit: field (%)?
– If no, go to step 6.
– If yes, go to step 4.
6. Dup.E alarm is issued for this result.
(e 801)

Roche Diagnostics
cobas® pro integrated solutions · Software version 03-03 · User Guide · Publication version 4.2

– If yes, go to step 4.

1036

Calibration data alarms

The difference between the first and second measurement
(absorbance) of a calibrator is outside the specified range.
The Dup.E alarm is displayed as Invalid on the automatic
Calibration Monitor report and on Calibration >
Results.

Cause

(CC)
•

The calibrator was dispensed incorrectly due to
leaking syringe.

(e 801)

Remedy

•

Air was aspirated during the first measurement due to
air bubbles on the corresponding calibrator. During
the second measurement, no air was aspirated.

•

Consequence: The signal values of the first and
second measurement differ more than the specified
percentage.

(CC)
1. Recalibrate.
2. Check the syringes for leakages.
3. Check reagent storage, handling, and expiration date.
Replace the reagent if necessary and recalibrate.
4. If the alarm recurs, contact your Roche Service
representative.

IStd.E
Alarm

Description

IS concentration abnormal

The concentration of the ISE Internal Standard solution
deviates from the specified limits.

Roche Diagnostics
cobas® pro integrated solutions · Software version 03-03 · User Guide · Publication version 4.2

Data alarms

1037

The concentration is checked by a relative and an
absolute check. The limits for both checks are specified on
Menu > Application > ISE > Calibration in the IS
Concentration area.

Cause

Remedy

•

Relative check: The deviation in mmol/L between the
current and the previous concentration must be
smaller than the deviation limit.

•

Absolute check: The concentration of the ISE Internal
Standard solution must be within the permissible
range.

•

If one of the checks fails, the IStd.E alarm is issued.

(ISE)
•

The flow path is contaminated.

•

The reagent has deteriorated.

•

The water quality is poor.

(ISE)
1. If the measured voltage of ISE Internal Standard
solution (IS EMF) is abnormal on the calibration
monitor report, check the ISE Internal Standard
solution volume. If necessary, perform a reagent prime
and recalibrate.
2. If the measured voltage of ISE Internal Standard
solution (IS EMF) is abnormal on the calibration
monitor report, check the condition of the ISE Internal
Standard bottle. If necessary, perform an ISE reagent
prime and recalibrate.
3. If the measured voltage of ISE Internal Standard
solution (IS EMF) is normal on the calibration monitor
report, check ISE reagent syringe. The measured
voltage of ISE Internal Standard solution ideally lies
midway between ISE Standard Low and
ISE Standard High.

5. Replace the ISE Internal Standard bottle and
recalibrate.
6. Check if all ISE tests are affected. If yes, replace the
ISE Internal Standard bottle and recalibrate. If only
one test is affected, check the status of the affected
electrode.
7. Check if the newest IS Conc. file is installed.
8. Resume operation. If the alarm recurs, contact your
Roche Service representative.

solution (IS EMF) is normal on the calibration monitor

Cause

Remedy

Response (ISE) abnormal 1

(ISE)

There is foam in the reagent flow path due to

•

The flow path is contaminated.

(ISE v1)

(pos. 3).

recalibrate the ISE analytical unit.

to 4 a maximum of 2 times. If the alarm recurs, replace
the ISE electrodes.

recalibrate the ISE analytical unit.

to 4 a maximum of 2 times. If the alarm recurs, replace
the ISE electrodes.

Remedy

(ISE)

QC data alarms

QC data alarms
QC data alarms indicate that a QC result is invalid.

In this section
QCHigh and QCLow (1048)
List of QC data alarms (1049)

QCHigh and QCLow
Alarm
Description

All analytical units

QC range over (upper)/QC range over (lower)
•

The QC result is outside the defined range displayed in
the Upper Limit and Lower Limit fields on QC >
Installation.

•

QCHigh: the QC result exceeds the value in the Upper
Limit field.

•

QCLow: the QC result is below the value in the Lower
Limit field.

Cause:
•

Improper preparation or storage of QC material.

•

Improper QC values (target mean, standard deviation)
or QC range.

•

Reagent is deteriorated.

•

Poor precision due to leakage in the sample pipetter
flow paths or reagent pipetter flow paths.

Remedy:

14 Data alarms

1. Check that the QC material is properly prepared,
positioned, and stored.
2. If you use laboratory-specific target values, check the
values on QC > Installation for the respective test in
the Target Mean or Target SD columns.
3. Replace the reagent pack.
4. Prepare new QC material.

1052

List of data alarms that generate an automatic rerun test

List of data alarms that generate an
automatic rerun test
The system automatically orders a rerun test when
specific data alarms are attached to a test result.
The table below shows the rerun test conditions.

Prerequisites for automatic rerun

To enable the execution of automatic reruns for a test, the
following settings must be activated:
1. For all tests: Start > Retain Rack in System for
Automatic Rerun
2. For the respective test: Menu > Application >
Analytical Parameters
If both settings are active, the sample remains on the
system until the first result for this test is available. This
enables the system to perform a rerun test automatically
without reloading the sample, if necessary.

Abbreviations

I

Rerun test is performed with an increased
pipetting volume.

N

Rerun test is performed with the same (normal)
pipetting volume (repeat test).

D

Rerun test is performed with a decreased
pipetting volume.

NR

No rerun is performed on this analytical unit.

-

Not applicable

1061

Adding a user to the system
To access the system, each operator and administrator
needs a unique user ID and password.
User ID

The system supports up to 100 user IDs.
privacy reasons, use alias names for user IDs
i For
(pseudonyms), not real names.
Delete user IDs from the system for users who no longer
work on the system.
A deleted user ID remains in the database system for the
user’s past activities.

Password

When you create a user ID, you must define an initial
password.
When the user logs on for the first time, the system
prompts to change the initial password to a personal
password.
If a user forgets the password, administrators can assign a
new initial password.

Password policy

if you have not selected any of the check
i Even

About rack ranges
For each rack you use, assign the corresponding rack
range in the rack range settings.

15 System settings

The system derives the following information, for each
rack, from the rack range settings:
Information

Examples

Container type

Standard tube, non-standard tube, false bottom tube, Sarstedt
Micro Tube

Container shape

Height, bottom level, tube bottom shape (only false bottom
tubes)

Sample type

Serum/plasma or urine, for example

y Information derived from the position of a rack ID in the rack range settings

a rack only with the containers and sample
i Load
types specified in the rack range settings.
The information derived from the rack range settings
complements the rack class information encoded in the
rack ID ranges.
The system needs all this information to process the racks
and the containers on them adequately, for example:
•

To process STAT racks with priority

•

To avoid crashing the sample probe into the bottom of
a false bottom tube

About columns for standard racks

u Types of standard racks (99)

About columns for rack classes (Routine/
Rerun/STAT)

Each rack class has a specific rack ID range. Use valid
rack ID ranges, for example, 50001–50999, for routine
racks.
You can split up a rack ID range and assign subsets to
different sample types, for example:
•

50001–50160 for serum/plasma routine samples

•

50161–50180 for hemolysate routine samples

Only assign rerun racks when you do manual rerun tests in
non-barcode mode.

tubes automatically. Assign a rack ID range for nonstandard tubes. Then the system determines all containers
on these racks as non-standard tubes, regardless of their
height.
Non‑standard tubes are tubes that comply to the
specifications for non-standard tubes.

In barcode mode, you can use barcoded and nonbarcoded samples. In non-barcode mode, you can only use
non-barcoded samples.

cobas® pro integrated solutions · Software version 03-03 · User Guide · Publication version 4.2

System settings

1081

The use of check digits ensures correct barcode reading.
Therefore, only use barcodes with check digits.
To avoid barcode read errors, ensure that the check digits
match the barcode types you use.
If you use the Codabar (NW7) check digit, from the dropdown list, choose the used modulus.
Code 128, there is no check box, as it always
i For
has a check digit.

Sample Type Encoding in Barcode
Encrypt sample type information within sample barcodes,
using up to 3 numeric digits.
If applied, you can load samples with different sample
types on the same rack defined under 22 Barcode on
Menu > System > Rack Ranges.
From the Position drop-down list, choose whether the
digits which encrypt the sample type are at the beginning
(First option) or at the end (Last option) of the sample
barcodes.
From the Digits drop-down list, choose the number of
digits which encrypt the sample types within barcodes.
Enter the numeric digits into the text fields for all sample
types used.
The rack range must be defined Menu > System > Rack
Ranges > 22 Barcode.

1101

the e 801 analytical unit, clot detection is
i For
always active, even with the setting disabled.

Reagent level warnings

Reagent level warnings
To help monitor the reagent status, the system provides
reagent level warnings. Define the thresholds for the
reagent level warnings to ensure continuous operation.

In this section
About reagent level warnings (1108)
Defining reagent level warnings (1110)

About reagent level warnings
Reagent level warnings occur when the remaining volume
drops below the defined thresholds.

Colors for reagent level warnings

Warning color

Purple

To indicate the different reagent level warnings, the
system uses colors. Define the thresholds for the yellow
reagent level warning and the purple reagent level
warning.

Trigger

Recommendation and required action

The reagent level is below the
purple threshold.

Set the threshold to 110% of the average daily consumption of
a regular working day.
At the beginning of the work shift, provide enough reagent for
the day.

Yellow

The reagent level is below the
yellow threshold.

Set the threshold to 10% of the average daily consumption of a
regular working day.
Provide new reagent as soon as possible.

15 System settings

Red

Reagent is empty, missing, or
masked.

Provide new reagent immediately.

The system cannot perform the
test that uses this reagent.
y Alarm colors of reagent level warning

purple reagent level warning only displays if
i The
you select the Preventive Action check box in
the Pre-Routine dialog box.

Thresholds

Define the thresholds for the purple reagent level warning
and the yellow reagent level warning.
The threshold represents the following:

cobas® pro integrated solutions · Software version 03-03 · User Guide · Publication version 4.2

System settings

•

Assay reagents (remaining number of tests)

•

ISE electrodes (remaining number of tests)

Consumption-Based Load List

System reagents

System reagents with 2 bottles

The Consumption-Based Load List can be generated
per weekday. It displays an overview of the average
consumption and the reagent needs, for the selected
weekday. The calculation is based on the actual usage
during the last 9 weeks. Days without consumption are not
included.
This report is helpful when the number of tests varies
between the weekdays, for example, because the
laboratory performs certain tests only on certain
weekdays.

1116

About Result Upload settings

About Result Upload settings
The system can send the results automatically to the host
in real time. The settings define the timing when the
system sends the result message to the host.
You can select the options individually for results of
routine samples, STAT samples, calibrations, and QC
measurements.
To open the Result Upload dialog box, choose Menu >
System > Result Upload.
If you select the As Soon As Setting check box, the
system uploads results to the host when all results for
tests having the automatic rerun setting enabled are
available. The host can send the orders for rerun and
repeat tests faster, which has the greatest benefit when
the By Sample option is selected.
The options in the drop-down lists have the following
consequences for the communication to the host:

data:
•

System configuration

The system supports 2 different methods of configuring
the SFTP connection to be used for network storage.
Before setting up a network storage, the following
information must be provided by the responsible IT
department:
Required information

the usage of a network storage, the Roche

15 System settings

Therefore, whenever a change in the network
storage configuration is planned, inform your
Roche Service representative.

The exported data is stored on the network
storage inside an automatically created folder,
whereby the folder name represents the serial
number of the SSU. This ensures a clear
differentiation of the exported data in case several
systems are connected to the same network
storage.
For automatic folder creation, the system must be
allowed to write to the root directory of the server
in which the network storage resides.

To set up a new c 703 test, download the parameter from
cobas® link, configure the application settings, load all
necessary reagent packs, and perform a calibration and
QC.

the installation. Use the multiple downloading function in
the following dialog boxes:

button. Edit and confirm the displayed confirmation dialog
boxes one after another.

1.

Press the Reagent Loader button and wait
until it stops flashing.
The cover opens automatically after the
reagent loader comes to the loading
position.

2.

If reagent packs were unloaded, check the
status indicators:

Loading reagent packs at
the c 703 analytical unit

: Manually selected for unloading.
: Empty or expired reagent pack.
: Temporarily unusable reagent pack,
choose the Alarms button.
3.

Remove the unloaded reagent packs.

4.

Load reagent packs. Choose the loading
destination.

5.

Press the Reagent Loader button.
To finish loading, press the Reagent Loader
button for more than 2 seconds.
Optional: To load more reagent packs,
press the Reagent Loader button for less
than 2 seconds.
: Successfully registered reagent pack.

16 Application-related settings

: Reagent pack could not be registered
because it is empty or has expired.
: Reagent pack could not be registered
because it is temporarily unusable (e.g.
application parameters are not yet
downloaded or the reagent disk is full).
Choose the Alarms button to check the
cause.

measuring samples

Deactivating a single ISE electrode

You may temporarily remove the assignment of an
individual ISE test so that this electrode is used as a
dummy electrode. Choose Menu > Setup > Test
Assignment, select the ISE analytical unit, and deselect
the corresponding ISE test. The corresponding electrode
is then grayed out on Reagents > Overview.

Setting up sample index tests
Sample index tests allow the identification of potentially
interfering factors like lipemia (L), hemolysis (H) or icterus
(I) in serum, plasma, urine, and CSF samples.

Roche Diagnostics
cobas® pro integrated solutions · Software version 03-03 · User Guide · Publication version 4.2

y Setting up a typical ISE test

1140

Setting up a test

Sample index values

The sample index is measured semi-quantitatively as
follows.
Sample index values

Interference

L

Lipemic index

Turbidity caused by lipids

H

Hemolytic index

Colorimetric and biochemical
interference from hemolyzed
blood cells

I

Icteric index

Colorimetric and biochemical
interference of bilirubin-related
compounds

y Sample index values

Application Correction Factor

Each application has specific interference limits. Refer to
the corresponding Method Sheet.

Sample Index Limits

A:

1.0

L:

1500

B:

0.000

H:
I:

1000
60

On Menu > Application > Ranges, the Sample Index
Limits area displays the interference limits for
photometric applications.
For ISE applications, the Sample Index Limits area is
displayed on Menu > Application > Reference Ranges.
If any measured sample index is above the applicationspecific interference limits, a data alarm is attached to the
result of the affected test.

j

m The system is in Standby mode.
m You are logged on as an administrator.

r To set up sample index
1 Choose Menu > Application > Download and
download the following applications for all desired
sample types:
• Ser/Pl: SI2 (29110), SI2-B (29111)
• CSF: SI2C (29120), SI2C-B (29121)
• Urine: SI2U (29130), SI2U-B (29131)
I For each sample type, both applications must be
installed. SI2x is used for the absorbance
measurement. SI2x-B includes the application for
L,H, I and is needed for the calculation.
Refer to the Method Sheet for the sample index
application in case the ACNs are not available.

Setting up a cobas® e flow test
cobas® e flow tests are an automated combination of
immunology tests.
cobas® e flow tests

cobas® e flow tests are defined combinations of
conventional immunological tests.

16 Application-related settings

Examples of test combinations:
•

A sequence of different tests based on previously
determined results.

•

A redundant measurement of one parameter with the
same immunology test.

•

A redundant measurement of one parameter with
2 different tests.

Essential parts of a cobas® e flow test are:
•

The algorithm which determines when to run which
immunology test.

•

The algorithm which determines how to calculate the
final result reported from the individual immunology
tests.

u About cobas® e flow tests - e 801 (528)
Embedded tests

The immunology tests performed as part of cobas® e flow
tests are called embedded tests.
You cannot order embedded tests manually, instead you
order cobas® e flow tests. Then, the system orders the
embedded test automatically.

Linked tests

Embedded tests that use the same reagent pack and are
dependent on one another are called linked tests. Linked
tests are pipetted in a set sequence.

Setting up a test

Setting up a non-Roche test
To install a non-Roche test, use Closed development
channel applications (CDC) that are handled with the tool
CDC File Creator.
Contact your Roche Service representative for more
information.

WARNING!
Incorrect results due to use of Closed development
channel applications
The use of non-Roche tests involves specific risks:
Errors during setup lead to systematically incorrect
results. The interaction between the reagents and the
cobas® c pack green is unknown. The stability and
onboard stability of the reagents is unknown. Errors
during filling the cobas® c pack green can damage the
instrument and lead to incorrect pipetting.
r For proper use of the Closed development channel
application, run QC tests regularly and monitor the
system during operation.
r For diagnostic purposes, always assess the results with
the patient’s medical history, clinical examination, and
results from other consultations.

After setting up a CDC application, define the necessary
special washes manually to prevent carryover between the
CDC reagents and other reagents.

Setting up reference ranges
Reference ranges

You can define the reference ranges for 2 genders (male
and female) in 3 different age groups per gender.
If a test result is outside the defined range, a data alarm (H
or L) is attached to the result and sent to the host.

Default values

You can define a default gender and a default range in
case no information is available for a sample.

1152

Setting up special washes

Setting up special washes
To avoid carryover between tests, the system performs
special washes. Depending on the combination of
reagents and samples, the probes and reaction cells are
washed to ensure reliable measurement results.
special wash parameters for all available Roche
i All
tests are already downloaded on the system. If you
install a new test, the system automatically
activates the required special washes.

Manufacturer Rules

The activated special washes are displayed in the
Manufacturer Rules table and are protected against
unintentional changes.
Special wash parameters are downloaded automatically
during Standby mode.
Afterwards the system issues an alarm to notify the user
about the update.

16 Application-related settings

You can define additional special washes for Roche tests.
If you use non-Roche tests (CDC applications), you must
define all possible special washes for reagent probes:

Special Wash for e 801

•

To protect the Roche reagents from potential
carryover, define the CDC reagent as offender.

•

Also define special washes for reagent probes with
the CDC reagent as victim according to manufacturer
information.

On the e 801, the sample probe uses disposable tips and
after each reagent pipetting step, a reagent probe wash is
performed automatically. Therefore, no special wash is
needed and the Special Wash dialog box is not available.

Roche Diagnostics
cobas® pro integrated solutions · Software version 03-03 · User Guide · Publication version 4.2

Application-related settings

1153

About special washes
To avoid carryover between tests, the system can perform
special washes. Download all required special washes
(Manufacturer Rules). For sample probes and reagent
probes, you can program additional special washes
manually (User Rules).
The control unit uses a random access system. Therefore,
reagent probes, sample probe, and reaction cells may
cause carryover and thus interference between tests and
samples, respectively.
In the e‑library, you can find the latest version of the
special wash list as an important note together with the
NaOHD-SMS-SCCS Method Sheet.

Sonic wash for sample probes

The following analytical units are equipped with a sonic
wash station for the sample probes:
•

ISE

•

c 503, S1 sample probe only

•

c 703

For special washes (in addition), the system washes the
sample probe with Basic Wash solution and optionally
ultrasound.

Special wash for reagent probes

The system only performs a special wash if the reagents
for the offender and the victim test are pipetted right after
each other with the same reagent probe.
Therefore, you must load the special wash solution only if
the reagents for both applications are loaded on the same
reagent disk.

Insufficient special wash solution

During preparation, the analyzer checks whether the
required wash solutions for the special wash rules applying
to the loaded reagents are available. The analyzer will not
start, if a wash solution is missing.
If a reagent, that leads to a special wash, is loaded during
operation and the required wash solution is missing:
•

The victim test will be masked

•

The offender test will still be processed

Roche Diagnostics
cobas® pro integrated solutions · Software version 03-03 · User Guide · Publication version 4.2

16 Application-related settings

After a certain amount of pipettings, the sample probe is
washed inside and out with Basic Wash solution and with
ultrasound (regular wash).

1154

Setting up special washes

If there is insufficient special wash solution during a run,
the corresponding analytical unit reacts as follows:

Special washes for HPI tests (e 801)

•

During sample probe wash: a Det.S data alarm is
issued, and the system enters the S. Stop mode.

•

During a reagent probe wash: a Det.S data alarm is
issued.

•

During a reaction cell wash: the reaction cells are not
used for measurement.

A subset of HPI tests has a manufacturer rule for
ultrasonic washing of sample probes on clinical chemistry
AUs. These tests are treated as non-strict HPI tests and
the sample can be processed first on any analytical unit.
For samples having non-strict HPI orders, the sample
probe is first washed with ultrasound before pipetting is
started. The system can process the non-strict HPI tests
on the e 801 analytical unit at any time. This allows the
system to react more flexibly when the e 801 has a high
workload.
u Related topics
• About strict and non-strict high-priority immunology
tests (HPI) (503)

16 Application-related settings

Defining a reagent probe wash
The reagent probes dip into the reagents when aspirating.
To avoid reagent carryover, you can define a special wash
for the reagent probe in addition to the special washes in
the Manufacturer Rules table.

i

•

A manufacturer-defined rule always has
priority and is followed.

•

Any user-defined rule having the same
offender and victim settings like a
manufacturer-defined rule are ignored.

About reagent cap conditioning – CC
Reagent cap conditioning (RCC) is a feature that allows
the system to automatically clean the caps of specified
reagent packs with pipetting-like movements.

Background

If a reagent pack remains unused for a longer period,
reagent residues remaining in the cap can lead to a
concentration of some reagent components. This
concentration problem applies to certain tests only.
Transferring the concentrated reagent into a reaction cell
would potentially lead to result deviation of the affected
tests.
To avoid transferring this concentrated reagent, the
system automatically cleans the caps of the
corresponding reagent packs based on the settings in the
RCC parameter file. The RCC parameter file, like the other
special washes, is distributed via cobas® link and
downloaded automatically during Standby mode.

i Ensure to use the latest RCC parameter file.

If an update is available, the system generates a
notification via Pre-Routine > Download
Required Items.

16 Application-related settings

•

The administrator can see the installed version and
release date on Menu > Special Wash > Cap
Conditioning.

About ISE technology
The ISE technology is used to determine ion
concentrations in diluted samples. The ISE analytical unit
uses 3 ion-selective electrodes to determine the ion
concentration of the sodium, potassium, and chloride.

Sampling area

A dilution vessel is used to mix different liquids such as
sample or QC material, ISE Internal Standard solution and
ISE Diluent solution. The liquids are mixed homogeneously
by discharging ISE Diluent solution into the vessel.
After measurement, the vacuum nozzle aspirates any
remaining liquid from the dilution vessel. The liquid is
drained into the outlet for diluted liquid waste at the back
of the system.

Roche Diagnostics
cobas® pro integrated solutions · Software version 03-03 · User Guide · Publication version 4.2

Measurement technology

Heating component

Several heating elements ensure the correct temperature
of reagents before they are ejected into the dilution
vessel.

Electrode block

The electrode block is the central component of the ISE
analytical unit. 3 ion-selective electrodes and a reference
electrode are available. The measurement is based on a
potential difference developing over the membrane of an
ISE. This potential determines the EMF measured against
the reference electrode. The resulting signal is processed
by the control unit.

Pinch valve

The pinch valve is involved in controlling the liquid flow
through the electrodes.

Syringes

Syringes are used to transport reagents and sample
material. Each liquid has its own syringe. The syringes are
filled with the respective reagents.

1175

The ISE Diluent syringe aspirates ISE Diluent from the
respective reagent bottle and dispenses it through the ISE
Diluent supply nozzle into the dilution vessel of the ISE
analytical unit. ISE Diluent is used to dilute samples at a
ratio according to the application settings specified in the
corresponding application file.
The sipper syringe aspirates diluted sample or ISE Internal
Standard solution from the dilution vessel into the
electrode block. After the pinch valve has been closed,
the sipper syringe aspirates ISE Reference Electrolyte
solution through the ISE reference electrode. The sipper
syringe discharges the aspirated solution to the drain port.

Liquid short sensor

A liquid short sensor is applied to the following: ISE
Reference Electrolyte solution (placed after the
degasser), ISE Diluent (placed after the degasser), and ISE
Internal Standard solution.

Degasser

A vacuum system degasses diluents and reference
solutions. Any gas that is dissolved in a reagent can distort
the measurement.

Roche Diagnostics
cobas® pro integrated solutions · Software version 03-03 · User Guide · Publication version 4.2

17 Measurement technology

The ISE Internal Standard syringe aspirates ISE Internal
Standard solution from the respective reagent bottle and
dispenses it through the ISE Internal Standard supply
nozzle into the dilution vessel of the ISE analytical unit.

Water

1178

About ISE technology

Discharging water into the dilution vessel mixes the liquids
homogeneously.
ISE Internal Standard solution is mixed with system water
in the dilution spiral. The diluted ISE Internal Standard
solution is then dispensed into the dilution vessel.
After measurement, the vacuum nozzle aspirates any
remaining liquid from the dilution vessel. The liquid is
drained into the outlet for high-concentrated liquid waste
at the back of the instrument.

ISE heating unit

The ISE heating unit ensures the correct temperature of
reagents before they are ejected into the dilution vessel.

Electrode block

The electrode block is the central component of the ISE
analytical unit with Na+, K+, and Cl- electrodes and a
reference electrode available. The measurement is based
on a potential difference developing over the membrane
of an ion-selective electrode. This potential determines
the electromotive force (EMF) measured against the
reference electrode. The resulting signal is processed by
the control unit.

17 Measurement technology

The ISE analytical unit has either 1 or 2 electrode blocks,
depending on the number of measuring units.

Pinch valve

The pinch valve controls the volume of liquid flowing
through the electrodes.

Syringes

Syringes are used to dispense specific reagents and
pipette sample material.
The sample syringe (Sample) aspirates sample material
from the sample container through the sample pipetter
and dispenses it into the dilution vessel.
The sample probe wash syringe (SPW) aspirates water
from the water container into the sample syringe to
support the accurate sample pipetting and sample probe
internal washing.
The ISE Internal Standard syringe (IS) aspirates
concentrated ISE Internal Standard solution from the
respective reagent bottle and dispenses it, after mixing
and/or dilution in the dilution spiral, through the ISE
Internal Standard supply nozzle into the dilution vessel.

application file.
ISE analytical unit has 1 diluent syringe per
i The

Overview of the test analysis workflow - ISE v1
A single ISE measurement sequence consists of 2
individual processes. The measurement of the ISE
Reference Electrolyte solution and of the Cl-, K+, and Na+
concentration is performed in parallel. A sampling cycle is
performed every 12 seconds.

Description

Start

1
1

Preparation

2

Initial ISE measurement

2
3

4

Measuring the diluted sample

ISE measurement

17 Measurement technology

End

3

At the beginning of each measuring sequence, the
dilution vessel is cleaned.
•

The ISE Internal Standard supply nozzle dispenses
ISE Internal Standard solution into the dilution vessel.

•

The vacuum nozzle drains the solution from the
dilution vessel.

Prior to sample measurement, the ISE Internal Standard
solution is measured.
•

The ISE Internal Standard supply nozzle dispenses
ISE Internal Standard solution into the dilution vessel.

About photometric technology
The photometric technology uses a photometer lamp to
beam light through a sample. A detector measures the
absorbance of the light. From this absorbance, the system
calculates the concentration of the analyte in the sample.

17 Measurement technology

A

1184

About photometric technology

figure represents the general characteristics
i The
of the photometric technology used in CC
analytical units. The c 703 analytical unit uses an
LED as its light source and has no heat ray cut
filter.

When the light beam enters the photometer unit, it strikes
a diffraction grating, which separates the light into its
constituent wavelengths. These are then reflected onto a
fixed array of 12 photodiodes. Each photodiode is
permanently positioned to detect light at a different
wavelength.
Absorbance readings are taken each time a reaction cell
passes through the photometer light path.
For every measuring point, the absorbance at the 12
wavelengths is measured.
Most Roche Diagnostics photometric tests use 2
wavelength readings to calculate results. The end product
of a chemical reaction absorbs the most light at one
particular wavelength. But sometimes interferences are
found when using a single wavelength (monochromatic
system). Using the difference between readings at 2
wavelengths (bichromatic system) eliminates the effect of
interferences and compensates for most of the
photometric interferences. The photometric resolutions
are therefore improved.

One of the bichromatic wavelengths is at or near the peak
absorbance of the chromogen produced by the reaction.
A second wavelength is chosen, where little or no
absorbance of the desired chromogen occurs.

Observed
Absorbance

17 Measurement technology

Chromophore

Interferent

Wavelength

Any absorbance (A2) that occurs due to interference from
other substances in the sample is measured at the
secondary wavelength. This amount is then subtracted
from the total absorbance (A1) occurring at the primary
wavelength to yield the net absorbance (Ac).
The optimum measuring points for each test are part of
the application settings, which are available via download.
The application settings determine how final results are
calculated for each test.

1191

About ECL technology
The electrochemiluminescent technology (ECL) used by
the instrument is based on the reaction of a ruthenium
complex with tripropylamine (TPA). A photomultiplier
measures the emission of light that emerges from this
reaction.

In this section
About the ECL measuring principles (1191)
Overview of the immunology test analysis workflow - e 801
(1195)
About advantages of the ECL technology (1197)

About the ECL measuring principles
ECL is a process in which highly reactive species are
generated from stable precursors at the surface of an
electrode. These highly reactive species react with one
another, producing light. The ECL processes are known to
occur with numerous molecules including compounds of
ruthenium, osmium, rhenium, or other elements.

The chemiluminescent reactions that lead to the emission
of light from the ruthenium complex are initiated
electrically rather than chemically. This is achieved by
applying a voltage to the immunological complexes
(including the ruthenium complex) that are attached to
streptavidin-coated microbeads. The advantage of
electrically initiating the chemiluminescent reaction is that
the entire reaction can be precisely controlled.

In this section
About the ruthenium complex (1192)
About the ECL reaction at the electrode surface (1192)
About the ECL signal generation (1194)
Overview of the processes in the ECL measuring cell (1194)

Roche Diagnostics
cobas® pro integrated solutions · Software version 03-03 · User Guide · Publication version 4.2

17 Measurement technology

The development of ECL immunology tests is based on the
use of a ruthenium(II)-tris(bipyridyl) [Ru(bpy)3]2+ complex
and tripropylamine (TPA). The final chemiluminescent
product is formed during the detection step.

1192

About ECL technology

About the ruthenium complex
ECL technology uses a ruthenium chelate as the complex
for the development of light. Salts of rutheniumtris(bipyridyl) are stable, water-soluble compounds. The
bipyridyl ligands can be readily modified with reactive
groups to form activated chemiluminescent compounds.

2+
O

N
N

N
Ru

N

N
N

O O

O
N

For the development of ECL immunology tests, a
N‑hydroxysuccinimide (NHS) ester of a modified
[Ru(bpy)3]2+ complex is used because it can be easily
coupled with amino groups of proteins, haptens, and
nucleic acids. This allows the detection technology to be
applied to a wide variety of analytes.

About the ECL reaction at the electrode surface

17 Measurement technology

Two electrochemically active substances, the ruthenium
complex and tripropylamine (TPA), are involved in the
reactions that lead to the emission of light. Both
substances remain stable as long as voltage is not applied.
The ECL reaction of ruthenium-tris(bipyridyl)2+ and
tripropylamine occurs at the surface of a platinum
electrode. The applied voltage creates an electrical field,
which causes all the materials in this field to react.
Tripropylamine is oxidized at the electrode, releasing an
electron and forming an intermediate tripropylamine
radical-cation, which further reacts by releasing a proton
(H+) to form a TPA radical (TPAo).
In turn, the ruthenium complex also releases an electron at
the surface of the electrode, thus oxidizing to form the
[Ru(bpy)3]2+ cation. This ruthenium cation is the second
reaction component for the following chemiluminescent
reaction with the TPA radical.

[Ru(bpy)3]3+ is reduced to [Ru(bpy)3]2+ and at the same time
forms an excited state via energy transfer. This excited
state is unstable and decays with emission of a photon at
620 nm to its original state. The reaction cycle can now
start again. The tripropylamine radical is reduced to byproducts, which do not affect the chemiluminescence
process. TPA is used up and therefore must be present in
excess. The reaction is controlled by diffusion of the TPA
and the amount of ruthenium complex present. As TPA in
the electrical field is depleted, the signal strength (light) is
slowly reduced once the maximum is reached.
Although TPA is depleted during measurement, the
ruthenium ground state complex is continually
regenerated. This means that the ruthenium complex can
perform many light-generating cycles during the
measurement process. Therefore, it shows an inherent
amplification effect, which contributes to the technology's
sensitivity. Many photons can be created from one
antigen-antibody complex.

About the ECL signal generation

Measured signal
Applied voltage

Viewed from an electrical perspective, the reaction of the
ECL signal generation can be explained as follows: When a
voltage is applied to the measuring cell electrode, a peak
of light emission occurs over a short time interval. This can
be detected as the resulting ECL signal. A defined area
under the curve is measured around the intensity
maximum.

Time

Overview of the processes in the ECL measuring cell
The ECL measuring cell is designed as a flow-through cell.
Essentially, 3 operating steps are performed:
•

Bound/free separation
The streptavidin-coated microbeads that are coated
with antigen-antibody complexes are uniformly
deposited on the working electrode by a magnet. A
system buffer (ProCell) is used to wash the particles
on the working electrode and to flush out the excess
reagent and sample materials from the measuring cell.

17 Measurement technology

•

ECL reaction
The magnet is removed and a voltage is applied to the
electrode to initiate the ECL reaction. The light
emission from the antigen-antibody complexes is
measured with a photomultiplier. The system then
uses the corresponding signals for the calculation of
results.

•

Release of microbeads and cell cleaning
Once the measurement is completed, the magnetic
microbeads are washed away from the electrode
surface with a special wash solution (CleanCell). The
surface of the measuring cell is regenerated by
varying the potential on the electrode. The measuring
cell is then ready for another measurement.

About advantages of the ECL technology
Electrochemiluminescence is a highly innovative
technology that offers distinct advantages over other
detection techniques.
•

Convenience of liquid reagents due to the stable nonisotopic label.

•

Enhanced sensitivity in combination with short
incubation times means high-quality tests and fast
result turnaround.

•

Large measuring range of 5 orders of magnitude
minimizes dilutions and repeat tests, reducing
handling time and reagent costs.

•

Applicable for the detection of all analytes, therefore
providing a solid platform for menu expansion.

1201

About test principles - ISE
The ISE unit performs indirect measurement of
electromotive force (EMF) in millivolts between ionselective electrodes and the reference electrode. Indirect
measurement means that all samples are diluted at a
dilution ratio specified in the corresponding application
files.
The EMF values of each sample are converted to mmol/L
values by a calculation algorithm that uses the EMF data
together with the parameter derived from an ISE main
calibration.
The Nernst Equation shows the basic relationship between
EMF (E) and activity of an ion.
z 1

E = E 0 + 2.303RT  z i F  lga i

ai

Activity of the ion

From this, it follows that for activity/concentration
determinations, a reference potential is required (E0),
which is taken before and after each sample
measurement.

The concentration of sodium, potassium, and chloride in a
sample is calculated from the EMF of the specific
electrode by the following equation:

1203

About photometric test principles - CC
analytical units
The photometric test principles apply to all tests that are
measured on CC analytical units and use absorbance
measurements for result calculation. This is true for
clinical chemistry tests as well as immunological tests.

In this section
About types of photometric assays (1203)
About how assays are displayed in the software (1204)
About data used for calculations (1206)
About endpoint assays (1208)
About rate assays (1212)
About high dose hook effect checks (1216)
About kinetic checks (1217)

About types of photometric assays
The photometric test principles used by the system are
split into 2 fundamental types, endpoint assays and rate
assays.

Measurements are taken by the photometer at specific
measuring points. If measurements are taken after the
reactions are completed, the intensity of the colored (or
turbidimetric) product is an indicator of the sample
component's concentration. These are called endpoint
assays.

Rate assays

With rate assays, measurements are taken as the reaction
proceeds. In this case, the rate of the reaction is
proportional to the sample component's concentration or
activity being analyzed.

Assay types

The fundamental assay types endpoint and rate are
divided into the following assay types:

Measurements used for calculation

Independent of the programmed application settings, the
system measures the absorbance of a reaction mixture in
the following fixed interval(s):
•

(c 503) 18 seconds

•

(c 703) 16 seconds (38 measuring points in 10 min)

However not all of the measurements are used for
calculating the result. Therefore, the numbering of the
photometer measuring points differs from the numbering
of the measuring points used in calculations.

About data used for calculations
The data used for the calculation of the various assay
types are displayed in different places of the software.
The Cell Blank Measurement Report contains data
necessary for the calculation of absorbance values, which
are the basis for all other calculations.
To display calibration information for individual tests and
calibrators, choose Menu > Application > Calibration
and Menu > Application > Calibrators. These windows
display data that is used for the calculation of the
concentration.
